label: ass:geometry
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:geometry}
The set $Q$ is nonempty, compact and convex, has an exact Euclidean projector, and has a known diameter bound $D>0$. Function values are available throughout $Q+\gamma_{\max}\mathbb B_2^d$, the evaluation domain. The population $f$ is convex and $M$-Lipschitz on this evaluation domain. Fix $x^0\in Q$ and a minimizer $x^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_Q f$ (one exists since $Q$ is compact), and let $R=\lVert x^0-x^\star\rVert$.

label: ass:vector
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:vector}
Let $G_\gamma^0$ denote the estimate \eqref{eq:record} computed
with exact function values ($\Delta=0$).
At every queried center and admissible radius,
\begin{align*}
 \mathbb E G_\gamma^0(z)&=\nabla f_\gamma(z),\\
 \mathbb E\|G_\gamma^0(z)-\nabla f_\gamma(z)\|^2
 &\le \sigma_\gamma^2<\infty.
\end{align*}
Whenever a uniform variance bound is used, assume
$\sigma_0:=\sup_\gamma\sigma_\gamma<\infty$, where the supremum
covers all positive radii permitted by the method, including initialization.

label: ass:conditional
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:conditional}
For the iterates and update estimates defined in
Section~\ref{sec:method}, let $\mathcal F_t^y$ and $\mathcal F_t^x$
denote the histories
immediately before the update batches at $y_t$ and $x_t$,
respectively. Each history contains the corresponding center,
the selected radius, the batch size, and all observations used
to choose them.
The history $\mathcal F_t^x$ additionally contains the
$y$-batch from iteration $t$, its estimate $g_t^y$, the resulting
projected point $v_t$ and averaged point $x_t$, and the
observations used to select the $x$-batch size.

Conditionally on the corresponding history, the function samples
and random directions in each update batch are independent and
follow the oracle's sampling distributions.
For each batch label $\iota\in\{y,x\}$, assume
$\mathbb E\|g_t^\iota\|<\infty$.
Define the conditional biases by
\begin{align*}
 b_t^y
 &=\mathbb E[g_t^y\mid\mathcal F_t^y]-\nabla\phi_t(y_t),\\
 b_t^x
 &=\mathbb E[g_t^x\mid\mathcal F_t^x]-\nabla\phi_t(x_t).
\end{align*}
The centered errors are defined by
\begin{align}
 g_t^y
 &=\nabla\phi_t(y_t)+b_t^y+\zeta_t^y,\nonumber\\
 g_t^x
 &=\nabla\phi_t(x_t)+b_t^x+\zeta_t^x,\nonumber\\
 \mathbb E[\zeta_t^\iota\mid\mathcal F_t^\iota]
 &=0,\qquad \iota\in\{y,x\}.
 \label{eq:conditional}
\end{align}
We assume
$\mathbb E[\|\zeta_t^\iota\|^2\mid\mathcal F_t^\iota]<\infty$
almost surely.
Additional unconditional moment requirements are specified
in the results that use them; in particular, a finite bound
in Lemma~\ref{lem:growth} requires its quantity $W$ to be finite.

label: lem:smoothing
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:smoothing}
For a convex $M$-Lipschitz population objective, $f_\gamma(x)=\mathbb E f(x+\gamma U)$ is convex and differentiable, with
\[
 \nabla f_\gamma(x)=\frac d\gamma\mathbb E[f(x+\gamma e)e],\quad
 0\le f_\gamma(x)-f(x)\le M\mu_d\gamma,\quad
 L_\gamma\le\frac{c_d M}{\gamma}\le\frac{\sqrt d M}{\gamma}.
\]
For each fixed $x$, $f_\gamma(x)$ is nondecreasing in $\gamma$. If $f$ is additionally $L$-smooth, then $L_\gamma\le L$ and
\[
 0\le f_\gamma(x)-f(x)\le L\nu_d\gamma^2/2.
\]
head: environment
name: Ball smoothing

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $C=Q+\gamma_{\max}\mathbb B_2^d$ and define
\[
 \bar f(x)=\min_{z\in C}\{f(z)+M\|x-z\|\},\qquad x\in\mathbb R^d.
\]
The minimum exists because $C$ is nonempty and compact and the integrand is
continuous. For $x\in C$, Lipschitzness gives $f(z)+M\|x-z\|\ge f(x)$;
the choice $z=x$ proves $\bar f(x)=f(x)$. Combining minimizers at two
points and using convexity of $C$, $f$ and the norm proves convexity of
$\bar f$. Evaluating at a minimizer for $y$ and applying the triangle
inequality gives $\bar f(x)\le\bar f(y)+M\|x-y\|$. Interchanging $x,y$
proves that $\bar f$ is globally $M$-Lipschitz, including when $M=0$.

For a smooth function, differentiation under the ball integral and the
divergence theorem give the displayed boundary identity: the
sphere-to-ball volume ratio is $d$. Convolve $\bar f$ with smooth kernels.
The approximations converge uniformly on compact sets, as do their ball
averages. For fixed $\gamma>0$, the boundary expressions converge uniformly
on compact sets because their difference is at most $d/\gamma$ times the
uniform approximation error. Integrating these gradients along line segments
and passing to the limit proves that the limiting boundary expression is the
gradient of the ball average. This argument applies at boundary centers and
at $\gamma=\gamma_{\max}$. On $Q$, the formula uses only values in $C$ and is
therefore independent of the chosen extension.

Convexity is preserved by translation and expectation. Jensen's inequality gives $f\le f_\gamma$. The Lipschitz inequality and the radial density $dr^{d-1}$ give $f_\gamma-f\le M\gamma\mathbb E\|U\|=M\mu_d\gamma$. For every unit vector $v$, the boundary formula gives
\[
 |\langle\nabla f_\gamma(x)-\nabla f_\gamma(y),v\rangle|
 \le \frac{dM}{\gamma}\|x-y\|\mathbb E|\langle e,v\rangle|
 =\frac{c_d M}{\gamma}\|x-y\|.
\]
Take the supremum over $v$. Rotational symmetry and Cauchy--Schwarz give $c_d\le d\sqrt{\mathbb E [e]_1^2}=\sqrt d$; integration of the spherical coordinate density gives the stated gamma-function expression (for $d=1$, both sides equal one).

The function $r\mapsto\mathbb E\bar f(x+rU)$ is even and convex, so it is
nondecreasing on $r\ge0$. In the smooth case, almost every ball sample has
$\|U\|<1$, and hence $x+\gamma U$ lies in the interior of $C$, even at
the largest legal radius. There $\bar f$ agrees with $f$ on a neighborhood,
so their gradients agree. The global Lipschitz bound justifies
differentiation under the integral and gives
$\nabla f_\gamma(x)=\mathbb E\nabla f(x+\gamma U)$. Averaging the original
gradient's $L$-Lipschitz bound proves $L_\gamma\le L$ on $Q$; no smoothness
of $\bar f$ outside $C$ is required. Averaging
$f(x+\gamma U)\le f(x)+\gamma\langle\nabla f(x),U\rangle+L\gamma^2\|U\|^2/2$
and using $\mathbb E U=0$, $\mathbb E\|U\|^2=\nu_d$ proves the last claim.
head: environment

label: lem:oracle-moments
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:oracle-moments}
Suppose the sample functions are locally Lipschitz on a neighborhood of the evaluation domain and their weak gradients satisfy $\mathbb E_\xi\|\nabla F(z,\xi)\|^2\le M_2^2$ on its interior, with the integrability needed for the following sphere and segment integrals. The clean estimate
\[
 G_\gamma^0(x)=\frac d{2\gamma}[F(x+\gamma e,\xi)-F(x-\gamma e,\xi)]e
\]
has mean $\nabla f_\gamma(x)$ and $\mathbb E\|G_\gamma^0(x)\|^2\le2dM_2^2$. A random sample Lipschitz constant $m(\xi)$ with $\mathbb E m(\xi)^2\le M_2^2$ is a sufficient condition. With fixed spatial corruption $|\delta|\le\Delta$, write
$G_\gamma=\nabla f_\gamma+b_\gamma+\zeta_\gamma$, where $\mathbb E\zeta_\gamma=0$. Then
\[
 \|b_\gamma\|\le c_d\Delta/\gamma,\qquad
 \mathbb E\|\zeta_\gamma\|^2\le2\sigma_\gamma^2+2d^2\Delta^2/\gamma^2
\]
whenever the clean centered second moment is at most $\sigma_\gamma^2$.
For a uniform bound, replace $\sigma_\gamma$ by $\sigma_0$. An average of $B$ conditionally independent records, drawn after the center, radius and batch size are fixed, has the same mean bias and centered second moment at most this bound divided by $B$.
head: environment
name: Moments and corruption of the symmetric estimate

title: Proof
body_md:
We first bound the clean estimate, then separate the corruption bias from
its centered fluctuation.

\emph{Mean.}
Taking expectation in the sample and using sphere symmetry gives
\[
 \mathbb E G_\gamma^0(x)
 =\frac d{2\gamma}\mathbb E_e[(f(x+\gamma e)-f(x-\gamma e))e]
 =\frac d\gamma\mathbb E_e[f(x+\gamma e)e]
 =\nabla f_\gamma(x),
\]
where the last equality is Lemma~\ref{lem:smoothing}. The integrability
hypotheses justify the exchanges of expectations.

\emph{Second moment for $d\ge2$.}
First suppose the samples are smooth and $\gamma<\gamma_{\max}$. The function
$h_\xi(e)=F(x+\gamma e,\xi)-F(x-\gamma e,\xi)$ is odd and therefore has
zero spherical mean. The spherical Poincar\'e inequality, with first
nonzero eigenvalue $d-1$, gives
\[
 \mathbb E_e h_\xi(e)^2\le\frac1{d-1}\mathbb E_e\|\nabla_S h_\xi(e)\|^2.
\]
The tangent gradient is
\[
 \nabla_S h_\xi(e)
 =\gamma(I-ee^\top)
 [\nabla F(x+\gamma e,\xi)+\nabla F(x-\gamma e,\xi)].
\]
Since $I-ee^\top$ is an orthogonal projector, the squared norm of this
expression is at most twice $\gamma^2$ times the sum of the two squared
gradient norms. Taking expectation in $\xi$ and $e$ yields
\[
 \mathbb E h_\xi(e)^2\le\frac{4\gamma^2M_2^2}{d-1},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\|G_\gamma^0(x)\|^2
 =\frac{d^2}{4\gamma^2}\mathbb E h_\xi(e)^2
 \le\frac{d^2}{d-1}M_2^2\le2dM_2^2.
\]

For locally Lipschitz samples, convolve with a smooth nonnegative kernel
of unit mass supported in a ball of radius less than
$\gamma_{\max}-\gamma$. Its translates at the queried endpoints remain in
the interior of the evaluation domain. Jensen's inequality and the
weak-gradient moment assumption preserve the bound $M_2^2$ for the
expected squared gradient of each convolved sample. The smooth argument
therefore applies. As the kernel support shrinks to zero, sample
continuity gives convergence of the endpoint differences. Fatou's lemma
then proves the same second-moment bound for the original samples.
This argument avoids evaluating weak gradients on a prescribed sphere.
The resulting dimension dependence also appears in the two-point
analysis of \citet{Shamir2017}.

\emph{Dimension one and the largest radius.}
For $d=1$, the fundamental theorem along the interval $[-\gamma,\gamma]$
and Jensen's inequality give
\[
 \mathbb E_\xi|F(x+\gamma,\xi)-F(x-\gamma,\xi)|^2
 \le 2\gamma\int_{-\gamma}^{\gamma}
       \mathbb E_\xi|F'(x+s,\xi)|^2\,ds
 \le4\gamma^2M_2^2.
\]
Thus $\mathbb E\|G_\gamma^0(x)\|^2\le M_2^2$ in this case. For any dimension,
let inner radii increase to $\gamma_{\max}$. Sample continuity gives
pointwise convergence of the estimates, and Fatou's lemma preserves
the second-moment bound at the limiting radius. The mean formula above
also holds there by Lemma~\ref{lem:smoothing} and the assumed
integrability.

The random-Lipschitz alternative requires Lipschitzness only on the closed
evaluation domain $C=Q+\gamma_{\max}\mathbb B_2^d$. Extend each sample by
\[
 \bar F(z,\xi)=\inf_{w\in C}\{F(w,\xi)+m(\xi)\|z-w\|\}.
\]
This extension preserves all queried values and is globally
$m(\xi)$-Lipschitz. Thus the preceding argument applies, and
$\mathbb E m(\xi)^2\le M_2^2$ bounds its gradient moments and endpoint differences.

\emph{Corruption bias and variance.}
Write
\[
 C_\gamma=\frac d{2\gamma}
 [\delta(x+\gamma e)-\delta(x-\gamma e)]e,
 \qquad b_\gamma=\mathbb E C_\gamma.
\]
For every unit vector $v$,
\[
 |\langle b_\gamma,v\rangle|
 \le\frac{d\Delta}{\gamma}\mathbb E|\langle e,v\rangle|
 =\frac{c_d\Delta}{\gamma}.
\]
Taking the supremum over $v$ proves the bias bound. Since
$\|C_\gamma\|\le d\Delta/\gamma$ and
$\zeta_\gamma=(G_\gamma^0-\mathbb E G_\gamma^0)+(C_\gamma-\mathbb E C_\gamma)$, we have
\[
 \mathbb E\|\zeta_\gamma\|^2
 \le2\mathbb E\|G_\gamma^0-\mathbb E G_\gamma^0\|^2
       +2\mathbb E\|C_\gamma-\mathbb E C_\gamma\|^2
 \le2\sigma_\gamma^2+\frac{2d^2\Delta^2}{\gamma^2}.
\]

\emph{Conditional batching.}
Condition on the observations fixing the center, radius and batch size
$B$. The $B$ centered update records have conditional mean zero and are
conditionally independent, so cross terms in the squared norm of their
average vanish. Its centered second moment is therefore at most
$(2\sigma_\gamma^2+2d^2\Delta^2/\gamma^2)/B$, while its bias remains
$b_\gamma$. The conditioning includes any separate diagnostic
observations used to select $B$.

label: prop:asymmetric
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:asymmetric}
For $\alpha>0$, $\beta\ge0$, define
\[
 G_{\alpha,\beta}(x)=\frac d{\alpha+\beta}
 [\widetilde F(x+\alpha e,\xi)-\widetilde F(x-\beta e,\xi)]e.
\]
Its clean mean is the gradient of
$\phi_{\alpha,\beta}=(\alpha f_\alpha+\beta f_\beta)/(\alpha+\beta)$, with $f_0=f$. Its smoothing bias is at most
\[
 M\mu_d\frac{\alpha^2+\beta^2}{\alpha+\beta},
 \quad\text{or, under $L$-smoothness,}\quad
 \frac{L\nu_d}{2}\frac{\alpha^3+\beta^3}{\alpha+\beta}.
\]
Its mean corruption is at most $2c_d\Delta/(\alpha+\beta)$; this is attained at a center when both radii are positive. For $\beta=0$ the stronger bound is $c_d\Delta/\alpha$. At the center of $f(z)=M\|z\|$, the clean second moment is exactly
\[
 d^2M^2\left(\frac{\alpha-\beta}{\alpha+\beta}\right)^2.
\]
head: environment
name: Nonsymmetric directional endpoints

title: Proof
body_md:
The boundary identity gives
$\mathbb E[f(x+\alpha e)e]=(\alpha/d)\nabla f_\alpha(x)$ and
$\mathbb E[f(x-\beta e)e]=-(\beta/d)\nabla f_\beta(x)$ when $\beta>0$.
For $\beta=0$, the latter mean equals $f(x)\mathbb E e=0$. Addition proves the target identity. Mixing the two smoothing bounds of Lemma~\ref{lem:smoothing} proves the bias claims. The dual norm argument in Lemma~\ref{lem:oracle-moments}, now with the coefficient $d/(\alpha+\beta)$, proves the corruption bound. At a fixed center $x_c$, the spatial function $\delta(z)=\Delta\operatorname{sign}\langle z-x_c,v\rangle$ attains it for any unit $v$ and positive radii. If $\beta=0$, the center contribution has mean zero, so only one endpoint contributes. Finally, the norm objective has endpoint values $M\alpha,M\beta$ at zero. Its estimate is the constant $dM(\alpha-\beta)/(\alpha+\beta)$ times $e$, proving the last identity. This instance concerns this estimator family; it imposes no restriction on other legal pairs.

label: prop:adjacent-scale
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:adjacent-scale}
Under the sample-gradient moment and sphere/segment integrability hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:oracle-moments}, one legal nonsymmetric pair at $x+\gamma U$ and $x+(\gamma/2)U$ gives
\[
 V_\gamma=\widetilde F(x+\gamma U,\xi)-\widetilde F(x+(\gamma/2)U,\xi).
\]
Without corruption its mean is $v_\gamma=f_\gamma(x)-f_{\gamma/2}(x)$, and
\[
 \tfrac12[f_\gamma(x)-f(x)]\le v_\gamma\le f_\gamma(x)-f(x),\qquad
 \mathbb E (V_\gamma^0)^2\le M_2^2\nu_d\gamma^2/4.
\]
Corruption shifts the mean by at most $2\Delta$ and gives
$\mathbb E V_\gamma^2\le M_2^2\nu_d\gamma^2/2+8\Delta^2$.
head: environment
name: An adjacent-scale paired diagnostic

title: Proof
body_md:
The mean identity follows from the same-sample sample expectation. Convexity gives $f(x+(\gamma/2)U)\le[f(x+\gamma U)+f(x)]/2$, and Jensen's inequality gives $f_{\gamma/2}(x)\ge f(x)$. These imply the bracket. Along the segment from $x+(\gamma/2)U$ to $x+\gamma U$, the fundamental theorem and Jensen bound the squared sample difference by $(\gamma^2\|U\|^2/4)$ times the average squared gradient norm on that segment. Integrating in $\xi,U$ yields the displayed moment bound. The two corruption values differ by at most $2\Delta$; applying $(p+q)^2\le2p^2+2q^2$ proves the last assertion.

The bracket concerns bias at the queried center. It does not bound smoothing bias at an optimizer: for $f(x)=|x|$ in dimension one and $x\ge\gamma$, $v_\gamma=0$, whereas $f_\gamma(0)-f(0)=\gamma/2$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:potential}
For every fixed $u\in Q$, the iterates
\eqref{eq:center-y}--\eqref{eq:coefficient} satisfy
\begin{equation}
 A_N[f(x_N)-f(u)]
 \le \tfrac{h_0}{2}\lVert u-x^0\rVert^2
       +2D^2(H_N-h_0)
       +\sum_{t=1}^Nt[\phi_t(u)-f(u)]
       +\sum_{t=1}^NZ_t.
 \label{eq:potential}
\end{equation}
If the total errors $e_t^y,e_t^x$ are integrable and satisfy
the conditional decomposition \eqref{eq:conditional}, then
$\mathbb E\sum_tZ_t\le D\sum_tt\,\mathbb E(\lVert b_t^y\rVert+\lVert b_t^x\rVert)$.
For batch means of \eqref{eq:record} with exact evaluations and
targets $\phi_t=f_{\gamma_t}$, $b_t^y=b_t^x=0$, and hence
$\mathbb E\sum_{t=1}^N Z_t=0$.

label: thm:formal-trajectory-potential
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:formal-trajectory-potential}
For every $u\in Q$, the execution
\eqref{eq:formal-trajectory-y}--\eqref{eq:formal-trajectory-H} satisfies
$x_t,v_t,y_t\in Q$ at their defined indices and $H_t\ge h_0>0$.
Moreover,
\begin{align}
 A_N[\phi(x_N)-\phi(u)]+\frac{H_N}{2}\lVert u-v_N\rVert^2
 \le{}&\frac{h_0}{2}\lVert u-x^0\rVert^2+2D^2(H_N-h_0)
       +\sum_{t=1}^N Z_t(u),
 \label{eq:formal-trajectory-potential}\\
 Z_t(u)={}&a_t\langle e_t^y,u-v_{t-1}\rangle
           -a_t\langle e_t^x,v_t-v_{t-1}\rangle.
 \label{eq:formal-trajectory-charge}
\end{align}
head: environment
name: Fixed-objective trajectory potential

title: Proof
body_md:
The weights in both centers are nonnegative and sum to one. Starting
from $x_0=v_0\in Q$, convexity and projection therefore imply all stated
memberships. The coefficient denominator is strictly positive and its
numerator is nonnegative, so induction gives $H_t\ge h_0>0$.

Write $r_t=\lVert v_t-v_{t-1}\rVert$ and $\delta_t=H_t-H_{t-1}\ge0$.
Projection optimality gives
\[
 a_t\langle g_t^y,v_t-u\rangle\le\frac{H_{t-1}}2
 \left(\lVert u-v_{t-1}\rVert^2-\lVert u-v_t\rVert^2-r_t^2\right).
\]
The two center definitions imply
\[
 A_{t-1}(x_{t-1}-y_t)+a_t(u-y_t)=a_t(u-v_{t-1}),
 \qquad A_t(x_t-y_t)=a_t(v_t-v_{t-1}).
\]
The convex gradient supporting inequalities at $y_t$ with
$x_{t-1},u$, and at $x_t$ with $y_t$, consequently yield
\[
 A_t\phi(x_t)-A_{t-1}\phi(x_{t-1})-a_t\phi(u)
 \le a_t\langle g_t^y,v_t-u\rangle+A_t\widehat\beta_t+Z_t(u).
\]
The scalar recurrence has the exact post-update identity
\[
 \delta_tD^2=[A_t\widehat\beta_t-H_tr_t^2/2]_+.
\]
To verify it, the nonpositive-numerator case has $\delta_t=0$;
otherwise multiply the update by its denominator and use
$H_t=H_{t-1}+\delta_t$.
Since $r_t,\lVert u-v_t\rVert\le D$, the resulting curvature remainder obeys
\[
 A_t\widehat\beta_t-\frac{H_t r_t^2}{2}
 +\frac{\delta_t}{2}\left(\lVert u-v_t\rVert^2+r_t^2\right)
 \le 2D^2\delta_t.
\]
Combining these inequalities gives
\begin{align*}
 A_t[\phi(x_t)-\phi(u)]+\frac{H_t}{2}\lVert u-v_t\rVert^2
 \le{}&A_{t-1}[\phi(x_{t-1})-\phi(u)]
 +\frac{H_{t-1}}2\lVert u-v_{t-1}\rVert^2
 +2D^2\delta_t+Z_t(u).
\end{align*}
Summation, $A_0=0$, $v_0=x^0$, and $H_0=h_0$ prove
\eqref{eq:formal-trajectory-potential}.

head: environment
name: Exact-gradient accelerated comparator bound

title: Proof
body_md:
Cauchy--Schwarz and the gradient Lipschitz condition give
$\widehat\beta_t\le L\lVert x_t-y_t\rVert^2$.
The center identity implies
$A_t\lVert x_t-y_t\rVert=a_t r_t$ and
$a_t^2/A_t=2t/(t+1)\le2$, hence
$A_t\widehat\beta_t\le2Lr_t^2$.
If $H_{t-1}\ge4L$, the update numerator vanishes.
If $H_{t-1}<4L$, its positive part is at most
$(4L-H_{t-1})r_t^2/2$, which gives
$H_t-H_{t-1}\le4L-H_{t-1}$.
Thus $H_t\le\max\{H_{t-1},4L\}$, and induction proves the cap.
In particular $H_N-h_0\le4L$. Exact gradients make every
$Z_t(u)$ zero. Drop the nonnegative terminal term in
\eqref{eq:formal-trajectory-potential}, substitute the coefficient cap,
and divide by $A_N>0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The membership and coefficient conclusions follow for each realization
from Theorem~\ref{thm:formal-trajectory-potential}. Consequently both
$u-v_{t-1}$ and $v_t-v_{t-1}$ have norm at most $D$.
Cauchy--Schwarz and integrability of the vector errors make both
error inner products integrable. The conditional-expectation pull-out
identity for the continuous bilinear inner product gives
\begin{align*}
 \mathbb E[\langle e_t^y,u-v_{t-1}\rangle\mid\mathcal F_t^y]
 &=\langle \mathbb E[e_t^y\mid\mathcal F_t^y],u-v_{t-1}\rangle=0,\\
 \mathbb E[\langle e_t^x,v_t-v_{t-1}\rangle\mid\mathcal F_t^x]
 &=\langle \mathbb E[e_t^x\mid\mathcal F_t^x],v_t-v_{t-1}\rangle=0.
\end{align*}
The two identities use their respective histories. Taking expectations
and multiplying by the deterministic weights yields $\mathbb E Z_t(u)=0$
for the charge in \eqref{eq:formal-trajectory-charge}.

Drop the nonnegative terminal distance in
\eqref{eq:formal-trajectory-potential}. Its remaining terms are
integrable by the assumptions and the preceding bounds. Take
expectations, use the finite sum of zero-mean charges, and divide by
$A_N>0$ to obtain \eqref{eq:stochastic-trajectory-expected}.

head: environment
name: Expected risk in terms of conditional variance

title: Proof
body_md:
Condition on the enlarged history after the current pilots. Its count
is fixed, and conditional independence and centering of the update
records imply
$\mathbb E[\|e_j\|^2\mid\text{enlarged history}]=V_j/B_j$.
Before the $x$ update, $e_t^y$ is known. Conditional centering of the
$x$ update therefore gives
$\mathbb E\langle e_t^x,e_t^y\rangle=0$. Expand each square and take
expectations to obtain \eqref{eq:batch-variance-exact}.

The recurrence \eqref{eq:batch-variance-scalar} is the fixed-target
execution of Theorem~\ref{thm:stochastic-trajectory-potential}.
Its two conditional-mean assumptions hold with the respective histories
before each update batch, including the current pilots and count.
Lemma~\ref{lem:growth}, with $L_\circ=L$, gives
\[
 H_N-h_0\le(4L-h_0)_+
 +\frac1D\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^Nt^2\|e_t^x-e_t^y\|^2}.
\]
The assumed second moments make this upper bound integrable.
The target is continuous on compact $Q$, so its objective differences
are also integrable. Thus all assumptions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:stochastic-trajectory-potential} are satisfied.
Apply that theorem, use Jensen's inequality and
\eqref{eq:batch-variance-exact}, and then use $f\le\phi$ to obtain
\eqref{eq:batch-variance-risk}.

For the adaptive batch rule, $\mathsf U\ge4N$ and
$1+\lfloor z\rfloor\ge z$ imply
$B_j\ge b_t\ge\mathsf U t/[4N(N+1)]=\mathsf U \omega_j/(8A)$.
Substitution into \eqref{eq:batch-variance-exact} gives
\[
 W\le\frac{8A}{\mathsf U}\mathbb E\sum_j\omega_jV_j
 =\frac{16A^2\overline{\mathcal V}_N}{\mathsf U}.
\]
The baseline total satisfies
$2\sum_tb_t\le\mathsf U/2+N\le3\mathsf U/4$.
All extras are nonnegative, and the remaining surplus is allocated
at final $y$; hence the update counts sum to $\mathsf U$.
Two pilots at each of $2N$ centers require $4N$ sampled functions, giving exactly
$T$ sampled functions and $2T$ values. Each iteration has a $y$ pilot stage, a $y$
update stage, an $x$ pilot stage, an $x$ update stage, and one projection.

label: prop:batch-variance-paid-limit
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Exact worst-case ratio of the adaptive batch rule

title: Proof
body_md:
Every feasible trace-comparator count satisfies
$n_j\le b_{t(j)}+S_{\mathrm{sur}}$, and $B_j\ge b_{t(j)}\ge b_1$.
Consequently $n_j/B_j\le1+S_{\mathrm{sur}}/b_1$.
Multiply by $v_j/n_j$, sum, and minimize over comparator counts to
obtain \eqref{eq:batch-variance-paid-upper}.

For the matching example, choose $m>0$, put $q_0=m/h_0$, and let
$Q=[0,D]$ with $D>q_0A_N$.
The population is $f(x)=-mx$, whose ball smoothing equals itself.
On a history of records all equal to $-m$, all pilot differences
vanish, the coefficient stays $h_0$, and no surplus is allocated
before final $y$. Projection is inactive. Directly from the scalar
step and averaging recurrence,
\begin{equation}
 v_t=q_0A_t,\qquad
 x_t=q_0(3t^2+7t+2)/12,\qquad
 y_t=x_t-\frac{2q_0t}{t+1}.
 \label{eq:batch-variance-affine-trajectory}
\end{equation}
Indeed, $v_t-v_{t-1}=q_0t$ and
$A_tx_t=\sum_{s\le t}sv_s$; the square and cube sums give the formula
for $x_t$, and $A_t(x_t-y_t)=t(v_t-v_{t-1})$ gives $y_t$.
For $t\ge3$,
\[
 y_t-x_{t-1}=\frac{q_0(3t-1)(t-2)}{6(t+1)}>0,
\]
while $x_t-y_t>0$, $y_1=0$, and $y_2=x_1=q_0$.
Thus the common centers have order
$y_1<x_1=y_2<x_2<y_3<x_3<\cdots<y_N<x_N$.
The initial $y$ center $c=y_1=x^0=0$ is unique among these centers.
Every other common center is at distance at least $q_0$ from $c$.
Choose a legal fixed $\gamma>0$ with $8\gamma\le q_0$.
Function values below are globally defined, so the required evaluation
domain is available.

For $r=x-c$ define
\[
 \psi_c(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 r,& |r|\le2\gamma,\\
 4\gamma-r,&2\gamma\le r\le4\gamma,\\
 -4\gamma-r,&-4\gamma\le r\le-2\gamma,\\
 0,&|r|\ge4\gamma.
 \end{cases}
\]
The formulas agree at their endpoints and have slopes of magnitude
at most one. Hence $\psi_c$ is globally $1$-Lipschitz.
Its symmetric secant at $c$ has slope one. Every other common center
has both radius-$\gamma$ endpoints outside the support, so its secant
has slope zero.

Fix $V>0$ and let the independently sampled variable $Z_p$ equal zero with probability
$1-p$ and equal $\pm\sqrt{V/p}$ with probability $p/2$ each.
Define the single time-independent sample function
\[
 F(x,Z_p)=-mx+Z_p\psi_c(x).
\]
Its mean is $f$, and its Lipschitz envelope satisfies
$\mathbb E(m+|Z_p|)^2\le2m^2+2V$ uniformly in $p$.
Population convexity is satisfied, and samplewise convexity is not
required. The one-dimensional symmetric record uses one sampled function
at exactly two points and equals
\[
 G_\gamma(z;Z_p)=-m+Z_ph(z),\qquad
 h(z)=\frac{\psi_c(z+\gamma)-\psi_c(z-\gamma)}{2\gamma}.
\]
It is independent of the sign of the spherical direction.
Its conditional mean is $-m$ and its conditional variance is
$Vh(z)^2\le V$ at every center.

Let $E_0$ be the event that all $T$ samples have $Z_p=0$, and put
$q_p=(1-p)^T$. On this event the complete trajectory and allocation
equal the common history. The only center on that history with
nonzero conditional variance is $c=y_1$; its weight is one.
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\sum_jv_j/B_j\ge q_pV/b_1.
 \label{eq:batch-variance-loss-numerator}
\end{equation}
On $E_0$, the trace comparator places all surplus at $c$, so its
value is $V/(b_1+S_{\mathrm{sur}})$.
On every trajectory, a feasible redistribution can only improve on
the baseline cost. Since $V_j\le V$ and $b_t\ge\mathsf Ut/(8A_N)$,
\[
 \mathcal C_\star^{\mathrm{tr}}
 \le\sum_j \omega_j^2V_j/b_{t(j)}
 \le16VA_N^2/\mathsf U.
\]
It follows that
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E\mathcal C_\star^{\mathrm{tr}}
 &\le\frac{q_pV}{b_1+S_{\mathrm{sur}}}
 +(1-q_p)\frac{16VA_N^2}{\mathsf U}.
 \label{eq:batch-variance-loss-denominator}
\end{align}
Choose $p>0$ with $pT\le1/(32A_N^2)$.
Then $1-q_p\le pT$ and $q_p\ge1/2$. The second term in
\eqref{eq:batch-variance-loss-denominator} is at most
$V/(2\mathsf U)$, which is at most the first term since
$b_1+S_{\mathrm{sur}}\le\mathsf U$.
Dividing \eqref{eq:batch-variance-loss-numerator} by
\eqref{eq:batch-variance-loss-denominator} proves the first inequality
of \eqref{eq:batch-variance-paid-loss}.
The baseline total is at most
$\mathsf U/2+N\le3\mathsf U/4$, so $S_{\mathrm{sur}}\ge\mathsf U/4$.
Also $b_1\le1+\mathsf U/[2N(N+1)]$, and hence
\[
 \frac{S_{\mathrm{sur}}}{b_1}
 \ge\frac{\mathsf U}{4+2\mathsf U/[N(N+1)]}
 \ge\min\left\{\frac{\mathsf U}8,\frac{N(N+1)}4\right\}.
\]
The reserve lower bound gives $b_1\ge\mathsf U/[4N(N+1)]$.
Together with $b_1\ge1$ and $S_{\mathrm{sur}}\le\mathsf U$, this
also proves the upper bound in \eqref{eq:batch-variance-paid-scale}.
Letting $p\downarrow0$ in the numerator and denominator bounds gives
a lower limit of at least $\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{batch}}$.
Equation \eqref{eq:batch-variance-paid-upper} bounds the upper limit
by the same value, proving \eqref{eq:batch-variance-paid-limit}.
The population and uniform second-moment envelope stay fixed.
When $\mathsf U=4N$, every $b_t=1$ and $S_{\mathrm{sur}}=2N$.
For fixed $N$ as $\mathsf U\to\infty$,
$S_{\mathrm{sur}}/\mathsf U\to1/2$ and
$b_1/\mathsf U\to1/[2N(N+1)]$, giving the final limit.

label: prop:variance-certificate
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:variance-certificate}
Fix $k<\infty$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$. No statistic that is finite almost surely on the all-zero sample, including a randomized statistic, can be an upper confidence bound with coverage $1-\alpha$ for the variance of every real distribution having finite second moment, using $k$ independent observations.
head: environment
name: A finite sample cannot bound an unknown variance uniformly

title: Proof
body_md: Let $U$ denote the proposed bound. On the all-zero sample choose a finite $K$ with $p_0=\mathbb P(U\le K)>\alpha$; such a $K$ exists by almost-sure finiteness. Choose $p\in(0,1)$ small enough that $(1-p)^k p_0>\alpha$. Consider a variable equal to zero with probability $1-p$ and $A$ with probability $p$. Its variance is $p(1-p)A^2$, which is finite and exceeds $K$ for sufficiently large finite $A$. The probability of observing only zero and producing $U\le K$ is $(1-p)^k p_0>\alpha$. On this event the proposed bound is smaller than the true variance. This contradicts the required coverage.

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $0\le q_t<1$, \eqref{eq:radius-policy-app} gives
$\underline\gamma\le\gamma_t\le\gamma_{t-1}\le\bar\gamma$ by induction. The resource condition gives $\mathsf U\ge T/2\ge5N\ge4N$. Summing the protected counts yields
\[

The account is exhausted at the last first center, so the update means consume $2\sum_t B_t^0+m_{\mathrm{sur}}=\mathsf U$ pairs. The $N$ radius diagnostics and $4N$ vector pilots give a total of $T$ pairs, each consisting of two scalar values.

The five successive stages in each iteration are the radius diagnostic, the first-center vector pilots, the first-center update mean, the second-center vector pilots, and the second-center update mean. Each stage uses functions and directions sampled independently of the completed history. Conditional on the completed radius and relevant vector diagnostics, the current center, radius, and count are fixed; the clean update mean is therefore conditionally unbiased for its smoothed gradient. label: lem:secant-growth
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Secant-curvature growth

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $\epsilon_t=\|e_t^x-e_t^y\|$. The scalar update's exact balance identity is
\[
 (H_t-H_{t-1})D^2=
 [A_t\langle g_t^x-g_t^y,x_t-y_t\rangle-H_t r_t^2/2]_+.
\]
If the update numerator is nonpositive, both sides are zero. Otherwise multiplication of the increment by $D^2+r_t^2/2$ and rearrangement prove the identity. Since $A_t(x_t-y_t)=t(v_t-v_{t-1})$, its right-hand side is at most
$[(\kappa_t-H_t/2)r_t^2+t\epsilon_t r_t]_+$.
Let $q=[\kappa_t-H_{t-1}/4]_+$. Monotonicity $H_t\ge H_{t-1}\ge h_0$ gives
$\kappa_t-H_t/2\le q-H_t/4$. Thus
\begin{align*}
 (H_t-H_{t-1})D^2
 &\le q r_t^2+[-H_t r_t^2/4+t\epsilon_t r_t]_+\\
 &\le q r_t^2+t^2\epsilon_t^2/H_t.
\end{align*}
The last inequality maximizes a scalar quadratic over $r_t\ge0$. Multiplying by $(H_t+H_{t-1})/D^2$, using $H_t+H_{t-1}\le2H_t\le2H_N$, and summing gives
\[
 H_N^2-h_0^2\le2H_N\mathcal C_N+2\mathcal E_N/D^2.
\]
Solving this quadratic inequality proves \eqref{eq:secant-growth-exact}. Subadditivity of the square root gives \eqref{eq:secant-growth-simple}.

For the uniform bound, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:growth} to the selected
targets with common bound $L_*$. It gives
$[H_N-4L_*]_+^2\le[h_0-4L_*]_+^2+\mathcal E_N/D^2$,
and hence $H_N-h_0\le4L_*+\sqrt{\mathcal E_N}/D$.
This proves \eqref{eq:secant-growth-uniform}.

\label{prop:protected-smoothing-smooth}
If $f$ is differentiable and $L$-smooth on the convex evaluation domain, every $f_\gamma$ is $L$-smooth on $Q$ and
\[
 0\le f_\gamma(u)-f(u)\le L\nu_d\gamma^2/2,
 \qquad \nu_d=d/(d+2).
\]

\[
 L_*=\min\{L,\sqrt dM/\underline\gamma\},\qquad
 \mathcal S_N(u)\le\frac{L\nu_d}{2A_N}
                       \sum_t t\,\mathbb E\gamma_t^2.
\]

\[
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le
 \frac{h_0R_u^2}{2A_N}+\frac{16LD^2}{N^2}
 +\frac{L\nu_d}{2A_N}\sum_t t\,\mathbb E\gamma_t^2
 +\frac{8\sqrt2\sigma_0D}{\sqrt T}.
\]

name: Smooth populations

title: Proof
body_md:
Differentiation of the bounded-ball average gives
$\nabla f_\gamma(x)=\mathbb E_U\nabla f(x+\gamma U)$. Smoothness on the evaluation domain implies
\[
 \|\nabla f_\gamma(x)-\nabla f_\gamma(y)\|
 \le\mathbb E\|\nabla f(x+\gamma U)-\nabla f(y+\gamma U)\|
 \le L\|x-y\|.
\]
The smooth upper model gives
$f(u+\gamma U)\le f(u)+\gamma\langle\nabla f(u),U\rangle
+L\gamma^2\|U\|^2/2$. Symmetry makes its linear expectation zero, and Jensen supplies the lower bound. Since $\mathbb E\|U\|^2=\nu_d$, the quadratic bias follows. Average this bound over the selected radii and substitute it and the valid smoothness bound in \eqref{eq:learned-radius-uniform-app}. No higher derivative is required.

label: lem:radial-affine
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Joint smoothing and a radial affine model

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the globally convex $M$-Lipschitz extension $\bar f$ constructed in
Lemma~\ref{lem:smoothing}. Its ball average defines $\Phi$ for all centers
and radii and agrees with the original smoothing on the legal domain.
All ball and sphere values in the asserted formulas belong to that domain.

For fixed $y$, let $q_y(s)=\mathbb E_e\bar f(y+se)$. This is continuous and
$M$-Lipschitz in $s$. Polar integration gives
\begin{equation}
 \Phi(y,\gamma)=d\gamma^{-d}\int_0^\gamma
                      s^{d-1}q_y(s)\,ds.
 \label{eq:radial-polar}
\end{equation}
The fundamental theorem of calculus applies to its continuous
integrand. Differentiating proves the equality in
\eqref{eq:radial-boundary} for every $\gamma>0$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:smoothing} gives the spatial derivative of $\Phi$.
Its sphere expression and the radial derivative just obtained are
continuous jointly in $x$ and positive $\gamma$: continuity of $\bar f$
gives uniform convergence of the integrands on compact parameter sets.
Thus $\Phi$ is continuously differentiable in the joint variables.
Both derivative formulas use only legal values when $x\in Q$ and
$0<\gamma\le\gamma_{\max}$, so they are independent of the extension.

For each fixed $U$, the function $(x,\gamma)\mapsto\bar f(x+\gamma U)$
is convex. Its expectation is jointly convex and
$\Phi(u,0)=f(u)$. Apply its affine lower model at $(y,\gamma)$
to $(u,0)$ to obtain \eqref{eq:radial-affine}. The segment in
this application uses only points of the original evaluation domain.

The radial function $\gamma\mapsto\Phi(y,\gamma)$ is convex and
even. Its derivative on the positive half-line is nonnegative and
nondecreasing. Its Lipschitz constant is at most
$M\mathbb E\lVert U\rVert=M\mu_d$, which proves the inequality in
\eqref{eq:radial-boundary}. Monotonicity of the derivative gives
\[
 h_{\lambda\gamma}(y)
 =\lambda\gamma\partial_\gamma\Phi(y,\lambda\gamma)
 \le\lambda\gamma\partial_\gamma\Phi(y,\gamma)
 =\lambda h_\gamma(y).
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:radial-shrink}.

In the smooth case, almost every sampled ball point is interior to the
original evaluation domain, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:smoothing}. Differentiation
under the integral therefore uses the original gradient, without requiring
a smooth extension. Symmetry gives
\begin{align*}
 \partial_\gamma\Phi(y,\gamma)
 &=\mathbb E\langle \nabla f(y+\gamma U),U\rangle\\
 &=\mathbb E\langle \nabla f(y+\gamma U)-\nabla f(y),U\rangle
 \le L\gamma\mathbb E\lVert U\rVert^2=L\nu_d\gamma.
\end{align*}
Multiplication by $\gamma$ proves
\eqref{eq:radial-smooth-charge}, without a higher derivative.

label: lem:radial-moment
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Radial mean and second moment

title: Proof
body_md:
The random point $re$ is uniform in the unit ball and independent
of $\xi$. Taking the expectation of the population difference in
\eqref{eq:radial-record} and applying
\eqref{eq:radial-boundary} gives its asserted mean. This uses the
difference, so a common random sample offset cancels.

The random Lipschitz envelope gives
$|J_\gamma|\le dm(\xi)\gamma(1-r)$. Under the weak-gradient
condition, the fundamental theorem on the radial segment gives
\[
 J_\gamma=d\gamma(1-r)\int_0^1
 \langle \nabla F(y+\gamma[r+s(1-r)]e,\xi),e\rangle\,ds.
\]
Jensen in this integral, followed by the gradient moment envelope
and Fubini, gives the same conditional squared bound
$d^2M_2^2\gamma^2(1-r)^2$. To justify the weak-gradient use,
local Lipschitzness makes every segment restriction absolutely
continuous. For almost every $\xi$, Rademacher differentiability
holds at almost every spatial point. Polar Fubini about each fixed
center shows that its weak gradient and the derivative along a
radial line agree for almost every direction and almost every
positive radius. Applying this statement to the sampled segment
gives the displayed fundamental theorem almost surely.
The moment envelope supplies the integrability used in Jensen and
Fubini. Finally,
\[
 \mathbb E(1-r)^2=1-\frac{2d}{d+1}+\frac d{d+2}
          =\frac2{(d+1)(d+2)}.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:radial-record-moment}.
Conditional independence of the records gives the variance and mean of
their average; its variance is at most the single-record second
moment divided by $B$. This proves
\eqref{eq:radial-mean-moment}. Each corruption difference is at
most $2\Delta$, so multiplication by $d$ proves the last claim.

label: thm:radial-potential
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Local radial potential

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $p_t^y=\nabla\phi_t(y_t)$, $p_t^x=\nabla\phi_t(x_t)$ and $\delta_t=H_t-H_{t-1}$.
We first derive an inequality for one update, then sum it while retaining
the changes in the smoothed target. The ordinary affine lower
model of $\phi_t$ at $y_t$, applied to $x_{t-1}$ with weight
$A_{t-1}$, and \eqref{eq:radial-affine}, applied to $u$ with
weight $a_t$, give
\[
 A_{t-1}\phi_t(x_{t-1})+a_tf(u)
 \ge A_t\phi_t(y_t)+a_t\langle p_t^y,u-v_{t-1}\rangle
                                  -a_th_{\gamma_t}(y_t).
\]
Here $A_{t-1}x_{t-1}+a_tu-A_ty_t=a_t(u-v_{t-1})$.
Convexity at $x_t$ and the center identity give
\[
 A_t[\phi_t(x_t)-\phi_t(y_t)]
 \le a_t\langle p_t^x,v_t-v_{t-1}\rangle.
\]
Projection optimality gives
\[
 a_t\langle g_t^y,v_t-u\rangle\le\frac{H_{t-1}}2
 [\lVert u-v_{t-1}\rVert^2-\lVert u-v_t\rVert^2-r_t^2].
\]
The curvature balance gives
$\delta_tD^2=[A_t\widehat\beta_t-H_tr_t^2/2]_+$,
with $\delta_t\ge0$. Since both $\lVert u-v_t\rVert$ and $r_t$ are at most $D$,
the curvature remainder satisfies
\[
 A_t\widehat\beta_t-H_tr_t^2/2
 +\delta_t(\lVert u-v_t\rVert^2+r_t^2)/2\le2D^2\delta_t.
\]
Substitute $p_t^\iota=g_t^\iota-e_t^\iota$ for $\iota\in\{y,x\}$ and combine these inequalities to obtain
\begin{align*}
 A_t\phi_t(x_t)+\frac{H_t}{2}\lVert u-v_t\rVert^2
 \le{}&A_{t-1}\phi_t(x_{t-1})
       +\frac{H_{t-1}}2\lVert u-v_{t-1}\rVert^2+a_tf(u)\\
 &+2D^2\delta_t+Z_t(u)+a_th_{\gamma_t}(y_t).
\end{align*}
Summing cancels the intermediate distance terms. For the target terms,
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{t=1}^N\bigl[A_t\phi_t(x_t)-A_{t-1}\phi_t(x_{t-1})\bigr]
 &=A_N\phi_N(x_N)-\sum_{t=1}^{N-1}A_t
             [\phi_{t+1}(x_t)-\phi_t(x_t)]\\
 &=A_N\phi_N(x_N)-\mathcal D_N.
\end{align*}
Use $A_0=0$, $v_0=x^0$, $\sum_ta_t=A_N$ and
$\sum_t\delta_t=H_N-h_0$. Discard the nonnegative terminal distance
term and write $\phi_N(x_N)=f(x_N)+[f_{\gamma_N}(x_N)-f(x_N)]$
to obtain \eqref{eq:radial-potential}.
The smoothing excess is nonnegative, and replacing the signed
drift by its positive part gives the stated simpler version.

Nonincreasing radii make the signed drift nonpositive by convex
evenness of the radial mean. To prove
\eqref{eq:radial-lipschitz-drift}, integrate
$\partial_\gamma\Phi\le M\mu_d$ on each increasing interval.
Integration of $\partial_\gamma\Phi\le L\nu_d\gamma$ gives
\eqref{eq:radial-smooth-drift}. Decreasing intervals have zero
positive contribution.

label: lem:radial-radius
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Local charge and reciprocal moments

title: Proof
body_md:
Condition on the history before the radial stage. Its center and
old radius are fixed. Write $h=h_{\gamma_{t-1}}(y_t)$ and
$\lambda=1/\max\{1,[\widehat h_t]_+/\tau\}$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-affine} gives
$h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)\le\lambda h$. Since $\lambda\le1$ and
$\lambda[\widehat h_t]_+\le\tau$,
\[
 \lambda h\le\tau+|\widehat h_t-h|.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-moment} and Cauchy--Schwarz bound its
conditional expectation by
$\tau+2d\Delta+\sqrt{\chi_d}M_2\gamma_{t-1}/
\sqrt{B^{\mathrm{rad}}}$. Using $\gamma_{t-1}\le\Gamma$
proves \eqref{eq:radial-selected-charge}.

The reciprocal update is exactly
$X_t=\max\{X_{t-1},[\widehat h_t]_+X_{t-1}/\tau\}$.
The normalized corruption is bounded by $2d\Delta X_{t-1}$,
so
\[
 X_t\le\max\{X_{t-1},
              ([\mathsf s_t]_++2d\Delta X_{t-1})/\tau\}.
\]
Fix a realized execution and let
$B=\max\{\Gamma^{-1},\max_t[\mathsf s_t]_+/\tau_-\}$.
If $X_{t-1}\le B$, the second term above is at most
$(\tau_-B+2d\Delta B)/\tau=B$. Induction proves
\eqref{eq:radial-reciprocal-path}.

Let $\bar s_t$ denote the conditional mean of $\mathsf s_t$
before the radial stage. Equations
\eqref{eq:radial-boundary} and \eqref{eq:radial-mean-moment}
give
$0\le\bar s_t\le M$ and
$\mathbb E[(\mathsf s_t-\bar s_t)^2\mid\mathcal F]
\le\chi_dM_2^2/B^{\mathrm{rad}}$. Therefore
\[
 \max_t[\mathsf s_t]_+\le M+\max_t|\mathsf s_t-\bar s_t|,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\max_t|\mathsf s_t-\bar s_t|^2
 \le\sum_t\mathbb E|\mathsf s_t-\bar s_t|^2\le \omega_{\mathrm{rad}}^2.
\]
Minkowski in $L_2$ bounds the norm of the slope maximum by
$M+\omega_{\mathrm{rad}}$. Apply
\eqref{eq:radial-reciprocal-path},
$\max\{a,b\}\le a+b$ and Minkowski once more to obtain the
second statement of \eqref{eq:radial-reciprocal-moment}.
Its first statement follows by Cauchy--Schwarz. This does not
require independence across iterations. Finally,
$B^{\mathrm{rad}}\ge T/(16N)$ and $\chi_d\le2$ prove
\eqref{eq:radial-public-moment-scales}.

title: Proof
body_md:
The radii are nonincreasing, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:radial-potential} has no positive drift cost.
Conditional centering gives $\mathbb E Z_t(u)=0$ separately at the two
histories preceding the respective sampling stages. For each realized execution, its targets have
the common smoothness bound
\[
 \overline L=\min\{L_{\mathrm{pop}},\sqrt dM/\gamma_N\}.
\]
The first alternative follows from averaging an $L$-smooth
population, as in Proposition~\ref{prop:protected-smoothing-smooth}.
The second uses Lemma~\ref{lem:smoothing} and the realized
minimum radius. The square-growth proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:growth}
is pathwise. Apply it after fixing the realized execution with
this common bound to obtain
$H_N-h_0\le4\overline L+\sqrt{\mathcal E_N}/D$.

The second centered update error has zero expected cross term
with the first, which is known before the second update mean. The
protected vector floors yield
\begin{align*}
 W:=\mathbb E\mathcal E_N
 &\le\sum_ta_t^2\sigma_0^2\mathbb E(1/B_t^y+1/B_t^x)
 \le16\sigma_0^2A_N^2/\mathsf U
 \le32\sigma_0^2A_N^2/T.
\end{align*}
The potential thus gives curvature contribution
$8D^2\mathbb E\overline L/A_N$ and stochastic contribution
$2D\sqrt W/A_N\le8\sqrt2\sigma_0D/\sqrt T$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-radius} and $\sum_ta_t=A_N$ bound the
local charge by $\tau+\eta_{\mathrm{rad}}$. Finally,
\[
 \mathbb E\overline L\le
 \min\{L_{\mathrm{pop}},\sqrt dM\mathbb E(1/\gamma_N)\}
 \le\min\{L_{\mathrm{pop}},\sqrt dM\mathfrak X_0\}.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:radial-main-risk} and its actual-trajectory
refinement. The required inverse-radius moments are proved in
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-radius}; no unexplained floor is imposed.

label: thm:radial-corruption
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Risk under spatial corruption

title: Proof
body_md:
At each selected vector center the corruption mean bias has norm
at most $c_d\Delta/\gamma_t$, and its centered single-record
variance is at most
$2\sigma_0^2+2d^2\Delta^2/\gamma_t^2$, by the symmetric-record
calculation in Appendix~\ref{sec:app-batches}. Write
$e_t^\iota=b_t^\iota+\zeta_t^\iota$ for $\iota\in\{y,x\}$, with conditionally centered $\zeta_t^\iota$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-radius} supplies the reciprocal $L_2$ bound
$\mathfrak X$. Therefore the weighted product-space $L_2$ norm
of $(b_t^x-b_t^y)_t$ is at most
$2c_d\Delta\mathfrak X\sqrt{\sum_ta_t^2}$.

The second centered error has zero expected cross term with the
first. The deterministic floor in \eqref{eq:radial-floors}
bounds their accumulated variance by
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_ta_t^2\lVert \zeta_t^x-\zeta_t^y\rVert^2
 \le\frac{16A_N^2}{\mathsf U}
        (2\sigma_0^2+2d^2\Delta^2\mathfrak X^2).
\]
This uses the fixed minimum batch size, without requiring independence between
the final inverse-radius maximum and a data-selected count. Set
$\overline V=2\sigma_0^2+2d^2\Delta^2\mathfrak X^2$.
Minkowski in the weighted product space gives
\[
 \sqrt{\mathbb E\mathcal E_N}\le
 2c_d\Delta\mathfrak X\sqrt{\sum_ta_t^2}
                       +4A_N\sqrt{\overline V/\mathsf U}.
\]
The expected potential bias, after division by $A_N$, is at most
$2c_dD\Delta\mathfrak X$. The first term of the error-energy
bound adds at most $4c_dD\Delta\mathfrak X$, because
$\sqrt{\sum_ta_t^2}\le A_N$. Their sum gives coefficient $6$.
The variance term is $8D\sqrt{\overline V/\mathsf U}$.
Use $\mathsf U\ge T/2$ and
$\sqrt{\overline V}\le\sqrt2\sigma_0+\sqrt2d\Delta\mathfrak X$
to obtain the last two terms in
\eqref{eq:radial-corrupt-risk}. The curvature and local charge are
bounded exactly as in Theorem~\ref{thm:radial-clean} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-radius}. No cross-term cancellation between
a second-center mean bias and the first error is assumed.

label: prop:radial-collapse
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:radial-collapse}
For $\tau,\Gamma>0$ and $2d\Delta>\tau$, there is a deterministic
flat population and a fixed spatial corruption of magnitude
$\Delta$ for which the proposed execution satisfies, almost surely,
\[
 \gamma_t=\Gamma\bigl(\tau/(2d\Delta)\bigr)^t,
 \qquad t=0,\ldots,N.
\]
Its vector records are all zero and its centers remain $x^0$.
Consequently the radial corruption bound $2d\Delta$ is sharp in
the stated spatial-corruption class. The conclusion concerns
inverse-radius stability; the original objective gap is zero.
head: environment
name: Collapse beyond the radial corruption margin

title: Proof
body_md:
Translate $x^0$ to zero and set $\rho=\tau/(2d\Delta)\in(0,1)$.
Take $F(z,\xi)=f(z)=0$ on any compact convex feasible set
containing zero and any evaluation domain of width at least $\Gamma$.
Fix before the execution the Borel corruption
\[
 \delta(z)=\begin{cases}
 +\Delta,&\lVert z\rVert\in\{\Gamma\rho^j:j=0,1,\ldots\},\\
 -\Delta,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
It is globally bounded by $\Delta$ and is independent of the
sampled functions and observation history. If the center is zero and the old radius
is $\Gamma\rho^{t-1}$, the radial outer endpoint is on a fixed
sphere and has value $+\Delta$. The inner endpoint has radius
$r\Gamma\rho^{t-1}$. Its continuous radial density gives zero
probability of hitting the countable set of fixed radii. Thus its
value is $-\Delta$ almost surely, and every radial record is
$2d\Delta$. The mean is the same, so the radius is multiplied
by $\rho$.

At the selected radius both endpoints of any symmetric vector
record have equal norm and equal corruption $+\Delta$. Their
difference vanishes. Hence the pilots and update means are zero,
the projection leaves $v_t=0$, and the averaged centers are zero.
Induction proves the displayed formula and the center assertion.
The samples have zero weak gradients and meet every stated clean
moment and regularity requirement. The flat population has zero
objective gap, so this is the claimed stability obstruction.

label: lem:threshold-accounting
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Accounting and diagnostic moments

title: Proof
body_md:
For $x\ge1$, $\lfloor x\rfloor\ge x/2$. Thus in both modes
$B^{\rm rad}\ge T/(16N)$ and $NB^{\rm rad}\le T/8$.
With fixed batch sizes $\mathsf U_{\rm pub}\ge7T/8\ge7N$, and
\[
 2\sum_tB_t^{\rm pub}\le
 2N+\frac{2(\mathsf U_{\rm pub}-2N)}{N(N+1)}\sum_t t
 =\mathsf U_{\rm pub}.
\]
The leftover for fixed batch sizes is nonnegative and its predetermined addition
makes the update counts sum exactly to $\mathsf U_{\rm pub}$.
Since $\mathsf U_{\rm pub}\ge4N$, their floors satisfy
$B_t^\iota\ge\mathsf U_{\rm pub}t/(2N(N+1))$ for $\iota\in\{y,x\}$.
With adaptive batch sizes $\mathsf U_{\rm emp}\ge5T/8\ge10N$.
The adaptive-batch accounting proof gives exactly $\mathsf U_{\rm emp}$ update
pairs and $B_t^\iota\ge\mathsf U_{\rm emp}t/(4N(N+1))$; the vector pilots
cost $4N$ pairs. Adding the $NB^{\rm rad}$ radial pairs gives $T$
in both modes. Each sampled function supplies exactly two values. Each iteration
has one radial stage and two vector stages with fixed batch sizes, or one radial
stage and four vector stages with adaptive batch sizes, and one projection.

The second vector error is centered conditionally on its history,
which contains the first error. Their expected cross term is zero.
The floors therefore give
\[
 \mathbb E\mathcal E_N\le
 \begin{cases}
 8\sigma_0^2A_N^2/\mathsf U_{\rm pub}
 \le(64/7)\sigma_0^2A_N^2/T,\\
 16\sigma_0^2A_N^2/\mathsf U_{\rm emp}
 \le32\sigma_0^2A_N^2/T.
 \end{cases}
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:threshold-energy}.

Let $\bar s_t$ be the conditional mean of $\mathsf s_t$ before its
radial stage. The radial moment lemma gives
$0\le\bar s_t\le M$ and conditional variance at most
$\chi_dM_2^2/B^{\rm rad}$. Hence
\[
 \mathsf S_N\le M+\max_t|\mathsf s_t-\bar s_t|,\qquad
 \mathbb E\max_t|\mathsf s_t-\bar s_t|^2
 \le\sum_t\mathbb E|\mathsf s_t-\bar s_t|^2\le\omega_{\rm rad}^2.
\]
Minkowski and Cauchy--Schwarz prove the two maximum-moment bounds,
without independence across iterations.
For the local charge set $\lambda=\gamma_t/\gamma_t^{\rm try}\le1$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-affine} and the threshold rule give
\[
 h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)\le
 \lambda h_{\gamma_t^{\rm try}}(y_t)
 \le\tau_t+|\widehat h_t-h_{\gamma_t^{\rm try}}(y_t)|,
\]
because $\lambda[\widehat h_t]_+\le\tau_t$.
Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the last expectation by
$\sqrt{\chi_d}M_2\gamma_t^{\rm try}/\sqrt{B^{\rm rad}}$
and hence by $\eta_{\rm rad}$.
The diagnostic floor, $\chi_d\le2$ and
$\Gamma\le d^{1/4}D/N$ prove
\eqref{eq:threshold-public-moments}.

label: lem:threshold-reference
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Reciprocal radii and geometric references

title: Proof
body_md:
The first relation follows from the trigger and monotonicity of
$\mathsf K_t$. Within a sequence of iterations having an unchanged
reference, the threshold is constant and the exact reciprocal update is
\[
 \gamma_t^{-1}=
 \max\{(\gamma_t^{\rm try})^{-1},[\mathsf s_t]_+/\tau_t\}.
\]
Its first trial radius is $\Gamma$; thereafter the trial radius is the
previous selected radius. Induction proves the inverse bound.
The smoothing bound $\sqrt dM/\gamma_t$ and
$\underline K_t>\mathsf K_{t-1}/2$ prove
\eqref{eq:threshold-smoothness}.
Each replacement raises the reference by a factor of at least two,
and its last value is at most
$\mathsf K_N=h_{\rm ref}+H_N-h_{\rm init}$.
This proves the event-count bound.
If its successive values are $c_{j-1},c_j$, then
$c_j\ge2c_{j-1}$ and $c_j\le2(c_j-c_{j-1})$.
Summation from the initial reference $h_{\rm ref}$ proves the
geometric-sum bound.

label: lem:threshold-growth
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Curvature under adaptive thresholds

label: eq:threshold-growth-square
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a complete realization. Its $\mathsf S_N$ and $\mathfrak H$
are fixed analysis quantities in this argument. Put
$a=\sqrt dM/\Gamma$ and $b=\sqrt dM\mathsf S_NN^2/D^2$.
The threshold $\mathfrak H=4a+2\sqrt2\sqrt b$ satisfies
\[
 \mathfrak H^2-4a\mathfrak H-8b=8\sqrt2a\sqrt b\ge0.
\]
Consequently, whenever $\mathsf K_{t-1}\ge\mathfrak H$,
\eqref{eq:threshold-smoothness} gives
$4L_t\le4a+8b/\mathfrak H\le\mathfrak H$.
If $\mathfrak H=0$, the population is constant and $L_t=0$,
so this conclusion holds directly.
The secant identity implies
$A_t\widehat\beta_t\le2L_tr_t^2+
t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert r_t$.
Use the single shift $\mathfrak B=\mathfrak H+2NM/D$ and
$k_t=[\mathsf K_t-\mathfrak B]_+$.
The balance identity has negative term $H_tr_t^2/2$.
Since $H_t\ge\mathsf K_t$, it is at least as strong as the negative
term using $\mathsf K_t$. Thus, when
$\mathsf K_{t-1}\ge\mathfrak H$ and $k_t>0$,
\[
 (H_t-H_{t-1})D^2
 \le[-k_tr_t^2/2+t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert r_t]_+
 \le\frac{t^2\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert^2}{2k_t}.
\]
As $0\le k_t-k_{t-1}\le H_t-H_{t-1}$,
\begin{equation}
 D^2(k_t^2-k_{t-1}^2)
 \le t^2\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert^2.
 \label{eq:threshold-growth-square}
\end{equation}
The case $k_t=0$ is immediate.
If $\mathsf K_{t-1}<\mathfrak H$, both true gradients have norm
at most $M$, and $r_t\le D$ gives
\[
 A_t\widehat\beta_t\le
 t(2M+\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert)r_t,\qquad
 H_t-H_{t-1}\le
 t(2M+\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert)/D.
\]
Then $k_{t-1}=0$ and
$k_t\le t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert/D$, so
\eqref{eq:threshold-growth-square} holds in this case too.
Summation yields $k_N^2\le k_0^2+\mathcal E_N/D^2$.
Use $k_N\le k_0+\sqrt{\mathcal E_N}/D$, together with
$\mathsf K_0=h_{\rm ref}$ and
$\mathsf K_N-h_{\rm ref}=H_N-h_{\rm init}$, to prove
\eqref{eq:threshold-growth-path}; the case
$\mathsf K_N\le\mathfrak B$ is direct.

By the diagnostic maximum bound and concavity,
\[
 \mathbb E\sqrt{M\mathsf S_N}
 \le\sqrt{M(M+\omega_{\rm rad})}
 \le M+\omega_{\rm rad}/2.
\]
Take expectations, drop the negative $h_{\rm ref}$ in the positive
part, and use \eqref{eq:threshold-energy}.
This proves the nonsmooth bound.
For a smooth population every target has the common bound $L$.
The original scalar-growth lemma, with initial coefficient
$h_{\rm init}$, gives
$H_N-h_{\rm init}\le4L+\sqrt{\mathcal E_N}/D$ and proves the
smooth bound. No independence between terminal maxima, chosen radii,
counts and curvature coefficients is required.

label: lem:threshold-drift
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Drift at radius reexpansions

title: Proof
body_md:
When $I_t=0$, the radius cannot increase, so its positive drift is
zero. On an event $I_t=1$, use $\phi_{t-1}\ge f$ and the radial
affine model at $(y_t,\gamma_t)$ applied to $x_{t-1}$. They give
\[
 [\phi_t(x_{t-1})-\phi_{t-1}(x_{t-1})]_+
 \le h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)+D_{\phi_t}(x_{t-1},y_t),
\]
where $D_\phi(x,y)=\phi(x)-\phi(y)-\langle \nabla\phi(y),x-y\rangle$
is a nonnegative Bregman remainder. The same right-hand side
bounds $\phi_t(x_{t-1})-f(x_{t-1})$.
The general upper bound for this remainder is
$2M\lVert x_{t-1}-y_t\rVert$; the smooth bound is
$L\lVert x_{t-1}-y_t\rVert^2/2$.
The center identity gives $\lVert x_{t-1}-y_t\rVert\le2D/(t+1)$.
Consequently
\[
 A_{t-1}D_{\phi_t}(x_{t-1},y_t)\le
 \begin{cases}2MDN,&\text{general case},\\LD^2,&\text{smooth case}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The exact coefficients are respectively
$2MDt(t-1)/(t+1)\le2MDN$ and
$LD^2t(t-1)/(t+1)^2\le LD^2$.

The event, center, trial radius and threshold are known before the
radial stage. Multiply \eqref{eq:threshold-local-charge}
by $I_tA_{t-1}$ before taking expectations. Since $A_{t-1}\le A_N$,
\begin{align*}
 \frac1{A_N}\mathbb E\sum_t I_tA_{t-1}h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)
 &\le\frac{D^2}{N^2}\mathbb E\sum_t I_t\underline K_t
                 +\eta_{\rm rad}\mathbb E J\\
 &\le\frac{2D^2}{N^2}\mathbb E(H_N-h_{\rm init})
                 +\eta_{\rm rad}\mathbb E J.
\end{align*}
The second inequality is the geometric-reference bound.
Add the Bregman remainder. This eventwise averaging makes no
independence assumption about the selected radius.

label: thm:threshold-risk
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:threshold-risk}
Assume the geometry of Assumption~\ref{ass:geometry}, the uniform clean
moments of Assumption~\ref{ass:adaptive-moments}, and the radial regularity
of Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-moment}. Fix $u\in Q$ and let
$h_{\rm init}\ge h_{\rm ref}>0$ be fixed in the initial history.
Choose $\mathcal H=\mathcal H_{\rm ns}$, or under population
smoothness $\mathcal H=\mathcal H_{\rm s}$, and put
$\ell=\log_2(1+\mathcal H/h_{\rm ref})$.
Algorithm~\ref{alg:threshold} satisfies
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le{}&
 \frac{\mathbb E[h_{\rm init}R_u^2]}{2A_N}
 +\left(\frac{2D^2}{A_N}+\frac{3D^2}{N^2}\right)\mathcal H
 +\frac{h_{\rm ref}D^2}{N^2}\nonumber\\
 &+\eta_{\rm rad}(1+\ell)+\frac{2MDN}{A_N}\ell.
 \label{eq:threshold-risk}
\end{align}
For an $L$-smooth population its last term may be replaced by
$LD^2\ell/A_N$.
Equivalently, each applicable branch is bounded by
$\mathbb E[h_{\rm init}R_u^2]/(2A)+\mathcal U_{\mathrm{reg}}(D,\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(D))$.
The method spends exactly $T$ pairs, $2T$ values and $N$ projections,
in $3N$ sampling stages with fixed batch sizes or $5N$ with adaptive batch sizes.
head: environment
name: A simultaneous threshold guarantee

title: Proof
body_md:
The radial potential of Theorem~\ref{thm:radial-potential}
holds with initial coefficient $h_{\rm init}$ by its projection
proof. Retain its positive drift term. Its two error inner
products have zero conditional mean at their respective sampling histories.
The weighted local radial charge satisfies
\[
 \frac1{A_N}\sum_t a_t\mathbb E h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)
 \le\frac{D^2}{N^2}\mathbb E\mathsf K_N+\eta_{\rm rad}
 =\frac{D^2}{N^2}
   [h_{\rm ref}+\mathbb E(H_N-h_{\rm init})]+\eta_{\rm rad}.
\]
This uses the conditional charge bound and
$\underline K_t\le\mathsf K_N$ pathwise.
Add the drift bound to the expected potential, obtaining exactly
the curvature coefficient in \eqref{eq:threshold-risk}.
Lemma~\ref{lem:threshold-growth} bounds the expected increase by
$\mathcal H$. Jensen and the event-count bound give
\[
 \mathbb E J\le
 \mathbb E\log_2\!\left(1+\frac{H_N-h_{\rm init}}{h_{\rm ref}}\right)
 \le\log_2(1+\mathcal H/h_{\rm ref})=\ell.
\]
Every coefficient multiplying the count is deterministic.
The eventwise diagnostic averaging precedes this logarithmic
bound, so no terminal-logarithm/noise product is introduced.
Finiteness follows from the vector and diagnostic moments and
the curvature bound. The initial coefficient can be conditioned
on its initial history throughout these arguments.

label: cor:threshold-smooth
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Unknown population smoothness

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the smooth form of \eqref{eq:threshold-risk}.
The identities $A_N\ge N^2/2$ and $A_N/N^2\le1$ give
\[
 \frac{2D^2}{A_N}+\frac{3D^2}{N^2}\le7D^2/N^2,\qquad
 LD^2\ell_{\rm s}/A_N\le2LD^2\ell_{\rm s}/N^2.
\]

\[
 \left(\frac{2D^2}{A_N}+\frac{3D^2}{N^2}\right)

 =\frac{c_{\rm vec}\sigma_0D}{\sqrt T}
       (2+3A_N/N^2)
 \le\frac{5c_{\rm vec}\sigma_0D}{\sqrt T}.

\eqref{eq:threshold-public-moments}. This proves the displayed
inequality. For the dimensional specialization use $R_u\le D$,
$d^{1/4}/\sqrt N\le\sqrt d$ and
$\sigma_0\le\sqrt{Cd}M_2$. None of $L,M,M_2$ is an input.

label: lem:corrupt-forward-secant
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Forward radial secant

title: Proof
body_md:
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-affine} proves that $(y,s)\mapsto f_s(y)$ is
jointly convex and differentiable at positive $s$, including evaluation domain
boundary radii. For fixed $y$, write $a(s)=f_s(y)$. Convexity yields
$a(2\gamma)\ge a(\gamma)+\gamma a'(\gamma)$, proving
$h_\gamma(y)\le q_\gamma(y)$. The radial function is even and convex,
so both quantities are nonnegative. Lipschitzness gives
\[
 q_\gamma(y)\le\mathbb E M\gamma\lVert U\rVert=\mu_dM\gamma.
\]
Its sample mean follows by taking the same-sample expectation at both
endpoints.

Under the gradient moment assumption, the fundamental theorem along the sampled
segment gives, almost surely,
\[
 \widehat q_\gamma^0
 =\gamma\int_1^2\langle \nabla F(y+s\gamma U,\xi),U\rangle\,ds.
\]
Jensen and Cauchy--Schwarz bound its squared magnitude by
$\gamma^2\lVert U\rVert^2\int_1^2\lVert \nabla F(y+s\gamma U,\xi)\rVert^2ds$.
The segment integrability assumption permits Fubini; integrating in
$\xi,U$ bounds the expectation by
$\gamma^2M_2^2\mathbb E\lVert U\rVert^2=\nu_dM_2^2\gamma^2$.
At an endpoint on the boundary of the evaluation domain, sample continuity
and increasing inner radii give the same conclusion by Fatou. The
uniform second-moment bound supplies uniform integrability for the
mean. Under a random Lipschitz envelope, instead apply
$|\widehat q_\gamma^0|\le m(\xi)\gamma\lVert U\rVert$ directly.

The two corruption values in the record differ by at most $2\Delta$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-affine} gives
$h_{\lambda\gamma}(y)\le\lambda h_\gamma(y)$, proving
\eqref{eq:corrupt-forward-shrink}. Its joint convex affine lower model
at $(y,\gamma)$ applied to $(u,0)$ proves
\eqref{eq:corrupt-original-model}. Finally, in the smooth case,
\[
 \partial_\gamma f_\gamma(y)
 =\mathbb E\langle \nabla f(y+\gamma U)-\nabla f(y),U\rangle
 \le L\gamma\mathbb E\lVert U\rVert^2=L\nu_d\gamma,
\]
where $\mathbb E U=0$ cancels the center gradient. Multiplication by $\gamma$
proves the last claim.

label: lem:corrupt-controller
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Protected radius and exact resource bounds

title: Proof
body_md:
The trial center and radius are fixed before sampling the diagnostic functions
and directions. The clean
normalized conditional mean is between zero and $\mu_dM$, and its
conditional variance is at most $\nu_dM_2^2/B^{\rm rad}$. Therefore
\[
 \mathsf S_N\le\mu_dM+
 \max_t\left|\widehat q_t^0/\gamma_t^{\rm try}
      -q_{\gamma_t^{\rm try}}(y_t)/\gamma_t^{\rm try}\right|.
\]
The squared maximum is at most the sum of the centered squared
normalized diagnostics. Taking expectations bounds its $L_2$ norm
by $\omega$. Minkowski and Cauchy--Schwarz prove
\eqref{eq:corrupt-diagnostic-maximum}.

The endpoint bound gives
$|\widehat q_t-\widehat q_t^0|\le2\Delta$ pathwise, hence
$[\widehat q_t-2\Delta]_+\le[\widehat q_t^0]_+$.
The exact reciprocal of the protected rule is
\[
 \gamma_t^{-1}=\min\left\{g^{-1},
 \max\left\{(\gamma_t^{\rm try})^{-1},
 \frac{[\widehat q_t-2\Delta]_+}
 {\tau_t\gamma_t^{\rm try}}\right\}\right\}.
\]
At the first iteration of every reference block the trial radius is
$\Gamma$; afterward it is the previous selected radius. Induction,
with the constant threshold in each block, proves
\eqref{eq:corrupt-inverse-path}. Since $\underline K_t\ge h_{\rm ref}$,
the pathwise maximum is at most $g^{-1}$ and at most
$\Gamma^{-1}+\mathsf S_NN^2/(h_{\rm ref}D^2)$. Taking its $L_2$ norm
proves \eqref{eq:corrupt-inverse-moment}. These arguments remain valid
when $g=0$, because all selected radii are positive.

Monotonicity of $\mathsf K_t$ and the trigger give
$\underline K_t\le\mathsf K_{t-1}<2\underline K_t$.
Successive replaced reference values increase by a factor at least
two, and the last value is at most
$\mathsf K_N=h_{\rm ref}+H_N-h_{\rm init}$. This gives the count in
\eqref{eq:corrupt-reference-cost}. For consecutive reference values
$c_{j-1},c_j$, $c_j\ge2c_{j-1}$ implies
$c_j\le2(c_j-c_{j-1})$. Summation proves its reference sum.

Finally $B^{\rm rad}\ge T/(16N)$ and $NB^{\rm rad}\le T/8$.
With fixed batch sizes, $\mathsf U_{\rm pub}\ge7T/8\ge7N$; summing its floors gives
$2\sum_t B_t^{\rm pub}\le\mathsf U_{\rm pub}$. Thus the prescribed
residual is nonnegative and makes the two-center update counts exact.
Moreover $B_t^\iota\ge\mathsf U_{\rm pub}t/(2N(N+1))$ for $\iota\in\{y,x\}$.
With adaptive batch sizes $\mathsf U_{\rm emp}\ge5T/8\ge10N$; the adaptive
surplus calculation gives exactly $\mathsf U_{\rm emp}$ update pairs
with $B_t^\iota\ge\mathsf U_{\rm emp}t/(4N(N+1))$. Its pilots cost $4N$
pairs. Adding the $NB^{\rm rad}$ radial pairs gives exactly $T$ in
both modes. Each sampled function contributes two values. Every iteration uses one
radial and two vector stages with fixed batch sizes, or one radial and four
vector sampling stages, plus one projection.
head: environment

label: lem:corrupt-vector-energy
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Biased vector energy and inner products

title: Proof
body_md:
At a fixed center and selected radius, decompose a single corrupted
symmetric record into its conditional mean and centered part. The
conditional bias is $b_\gamma$. The dual-norm calculation gives
$\lVert b_\gamma\rVert\le c_d\Delta/\gamma$.
The corruption vector has pointwise norm at most $d\Delta/\gamma$.
Its centered $L_2$ norm is therefore at most the same bound.
Minkowski with the clean centered record proves that the corrupted
centered standard deviation is at most $\sigma_0+d\Delta/\gamma$.
A mean of conditionally independent records has variance equal to the
single-record variance divided by its batch size.

For $\iota\in\{y,x\}$, write $e_t^\iota=b_t^\iota+n_t^\iota$,
where $n_t^\iota=\zeta_t^\iota$ in the notation of
\eqref{eq:conditional} and is centered conditionally on the history preceding
that update mean. The second history
contains the first centered mean, so
$\mathbb E\langle n_t^x,n_t^y\rangle=0$. The expected centered energy is bounded
using the deterministic lower batch floors. Since
\eqref{eq:corrupt-inverse-moment} implies
\[
 \left\|\sigma_0+d\Delta\gamma_t^{-1}\right\|_{L_2}
 \le\bar\sigma,
\]
the floor sums give
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_t t^2\lVert n_t^x-n_t^y\rVert^2\le
 \begin{cases}
 8\bar\sigma^2A^2/\mathsf U_{\rm pub}
          \le(64/7)\bar\sigma^2A^2/T,\\
 16\bar\sigma^2A^2/\mathsf U_{\rm emp}
          \le32\bar\sigma^2A^2/T.
 \end{cases}
\]
Here the randomness of $B_t^\iota$ is harmless because its deterministic
floor holds after the pilot observations choose it.
Both biases have norm at most $c_d\Delta\gamma_t^{-1}$, so
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_t t^2\lVert b_t^x-b_t^y\rVert^2\le4\beta^2\mathsf W_{N,2}.
\]
Minkowski in the weighted vector $L_2$ space proves the energy bound.
This decomposition retains all bias/noise correlations; it cancels
only the cross term between the two centered update means.

The vector $u-v_{t-1}$ precedes $n_t^y$, and $v_t-v_{t-1}$ precedes
$n_t^x$. Their two centered inner products vanish separately.
Each of these displacements has norm at most $D$, and
$\mathbb E\lVert b_t^\iota\rVert\le\beta$. Thus
$|\mathbb E Z_t|\le2tD\beta$. Summation uses $\sum_t t=A$ and proves
the second claim.
head: environment

label: lem:corrupt-local-charge
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Protected local charge

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $q=q_{\gamma_t^{\rm try}}(y_t)$,
$p=[\widehat q_t-2\Delta]_+$, and
$\lambda=1/\max\{1,p/\tau_t\}$. The endpoint bound implies
\[
 q\le\widehat q_t^0+
      |\widehat q_t^0-q|
 \le p+4\Delta+|\widehat q_t^0-q|.
\]
Indeed $\widehat q_t^0\le\widehat q_t+2\Delta\le p+4\Delta$.
If the floor is inactive, Lemma~\ref{lem:corrupt-forward-secant}
gives $h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)\le\lambda q$. Since
$\lambda p\le\tau_t$ and $\lambda\le1$, this is at most
$\tau_t+4\Delta+|\widehat q_t^0-q|$.
If the floor is active, $h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)=h_g(y_t)\le w_{\mathrm{reg}}$.
Either case is bounded by their sum.
The conditional standard deviation of the clean mean is at most
$\sqrt{\nu_d}M_2\gamma_t^{\rm try}/\sqrt{B^{\rm rad}}\le\eta$.
Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz now proves
\eqref{eq:corrupt-local-charge}.

label: lem:corrupt-growth-drift
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Protected coefficient and target drift

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a realization, and put
$a=c_dM/\Gamma$, $b=c_dM\mathsf S_NN^2/D^2$ and
$\mathfrak H=4a+2\sqrt{2b}$. The radius bound and
$\underline K_t>\mathsf K_{t-1}/2$ imply
\[
 L_t\le a+2b/\mathsf K_{t-1}.
\]
Moreover
$\mathfrak H^2-4a\mathfrak H-8b=8\sqrt2a\sqrt b\ge0$.
Thus $\mathsf K_{t-1}\ge\mathfrak H$ implies
$4L_t\le\mathfrak H$; if $\mathfrak H=0$, the population is
constant and this statement holds directly.

Use the unified shift $\mathfrak B=\mathfrak H+2NM/D$ and
$k_t=[\mathsf K_t-\mathfrak B]_+$. The scalar balance identity
and $H_t\ge\mathsf K_t$ give, when
$\mathsf K_{t-1}\ge\mathfrak H$ and $k_t>0$,
\[
 (H_t-H_{t-1})D^2
 \le[-k_tr_t^2/2+t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert r_t]_+
 \le\frac{t^2\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert^2}{2k_t}.
\]
Here the observed secant is bounded by
$A_t\widehat\beta_t\le2L_tr_t^2+
t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert r_t$, exactly as in the original scalar-growth
proof. Since $0\le k_t-k_{t-1}\le H_t-H_{t-1}$, it follows that
\begin{equation}
 D^2(k_t^2-k_{t-1}^2)\le t^2\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert^2.
 \label{eq:corrupt-square-recursion}
\end{equation}
The case $k_t=0$ is immediate. If
$\mathsf K_{t-1}<\mathfrak H$, both true gradients have norm at
most $M$, and $r_t\le D$ bounds the coefficient increment by
$t(2M+\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert)/D$. Then $k_{t-1}=0$ and
$k_t\le t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert/D$, proving the same recursion.
Summation gives
\[
 H_N-h_{\rm init}
 \le(\mathfrak H+2NM/D-h_{\rm ref})_+
                        +\sqrt{\mathcal E_N}/D.
\]
Take expectations, use
$\mathbb E\sqrt{M\mathsf S_N}\le\sqrt{M(\mu_dM+\omega)}$, and apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:corrupt-vector-energy}. This proves the nonsmooth
envelope. Under common population smoothness every target is
$L$-smooth; the original scalar-growth argument gives
$H_N-h_{\rm init}\le4L+\sqrt{\mathcal E_N}/D$, proving the
smooth envelope. Jensen and \eqref{eq:corrupt-reference-cost} yield
$\mathbb E J\le\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta$.

When $I_t=0$, the protected radius cannot increase: its candidate is
at most the previous radius and its floor also is at most that radius.
Thus only reference events have positive target drift. On such an
event the original affine model and $f_{\gamma_{t-1}}\ge f$ give
\[
 [f_{\gamma_t}(x_{t-1})-f_{\gamma_{t-1}}(x_{t-1})]_+
 \le h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)
 +D_{f_{\gamma_t}}(x_{t-1},y_t),
\]
where $D_\phi(x,y)=\phi(x)-\phi(y)-\langle \nabla\phi(y),x-y\rangle$.
The center identity gives
$\lVert x_{t-1}-y_t\rVert\le2D/(t+1)$. The Bregman remainder is
at most $2M\lVert x_{t-1}-y_t\rVert$, or
$L\lVert x_{t-1}-y_t\rVert^2/2$ in the smooth case. After multiplication
by $A_{t-1}$ these bounds are respectively at most $2MDN$ and
$LD^2$, that is $Aq_{\mathrm{reg}}$.

The event and threshold are predictable before the radial
stage. Multiply \eqref{eq:corrupt-local-charge} by $I_tA_{t-1}$
before taking expectations. Since $A_{t-1}\le A$ and the reference
sum is at most $2(H_N-h_{\rm init})$, this gives
\[
 \frac1A\mathbb E\sum_t I_tA_{t-1}h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)
 \le\frac{2D^2}{N^2}\mathbb E(H_N-h_{\rm init})
                      +(\eta+4\Delta+w_{\mathrm{reg}})\mathbb E J.
\]
Adding the Bregman sum and applying the two envelope bounds proves
\eqref{eq:corrupt-drift}. No terminal event count is multiplied by
an earlier random diagnostic error.
head: environment

label: thm:corrupt-radial
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Corruption-protected adaptive smoothing

title: Proof
body_md:
The scalar projection potential is a pathwise statement for arbitrary
observed vector records. Its derivation uses the same selected target
at both centers and the original-objective affine model. Those
conditions hold here. Therefore the changing-target potential is
\begin{align*}
 A[f(x_N)-f(u)]\le{}&
 \frac{h_{\rm init}R_u^2}{2}+2D^2(H_N-h_{\rm init})
 +\sum_t t h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)\\
 &+\mathcal D_N^++\sum_t Z_t.
\end{align*}
This is Theorem~\ref{thm:radial-potential} with its proved arbitrary
vector-error inner products retained; it requires no centering
assumption in the pathwise inequality.
Predictable local-charge averaging and
$\underline K_t\le\mathsf K_N$ give
\[
 \frac1A\sum_t t\mathbb E h_{\gamma_t}(y_t)
 \le\frac{D^2}{N^2}
 [h_{\rm ref}+\mathbb E(H_N-h_{\rm init})]+\eta+4\Delta+w_{\mathrm{reg}}.
\]
Add \eqref{eq:corrupt-drift} and the biased inner-product bound
\eqref{eq:corrupt-vector-energy}, and use
$\mathbb E(H_N-h_{\rm init})\le\mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}$ and $\mathbb E J\le\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta$.
The three local/drift coefficient contributions are
$2D^2/A+D^2/N^2+2D^2/N^2=k_ND^2$, giving exactly
\eqref{eq:corrupt-adaptive-risk}.
All terms are integrable by Lemmas~\ref{lem:corrupt-controller} and
\ref{lem:corrupt-vector-energy}, and the coefficient envelope.
An initial observed coefficient can be conditioned on its initial
history throughout. The cost claim is
Lemma~\ref{lem:corrupt-controller}.

label: cor:corrupt-bias-budget
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Protected bias budget

title: Proof
body_md:
For positive $\Delta$, the inverse-radius bound is at most $g^{-1}$,
so \eqref{eq:corrupt-public-floor} gives
$\beta\le\rho/D$ and
$\bar\sigma\le\sigma_0+(d/c_d)\rho/D$.
Since $A\ge N^2/2$, $A/N^2\le1$, and $\mathsf W_{N,2}\le N^3$,
\begin{align*}
 k_ND^2\frac{c_{\rm vec}\bar\sigma A}{D\sqrt T}
 &\le\frac{5c_{\rm vec}\bar\sigma D}{\sqrt T},\\
 k_ND^2\frac{2\beta\sqrt{\mathsf W_{N,2}}}D
 &\le\frac{14D\beta}{\sqrt N}.
\end{align*}
The direct inner-product term is at most $2\rho$.
The smooth deterministic envelope gives
$4Lk_ND^2\le28LD^2/N^2$ and
$q_{\rm s}\ell_{\rm s}^\Delta\le2L\ell_{\rm s}^\Delta D^2/N^2$.
These inequalities prove \eqref{eq:corrupt-smooth-explicit}.

For the nonsmooth branch,
\[
 \sqrt{M(\mu_dM+\omega)}\le\sqrt{M(M+\omega)}
                                     \le M+\omega/2.
\]
Also $k_N\le7/N^2$, $\Gamma\ge\Gamma_0$, and
\[
 \Gamma^{-1}\le2/\gamma_{\max}+N/(d^{1/4}D),\qquad
 \omega\le4\sqrt{\nu_d}M_2N/\sqrt T\le4M_2N/\sqrt T.
\]
The deterministic coefficients are therefore bounded by
$56c_dMD^2/(\gamma_{\max} N^2)$ and
$(28c_d/d^{1/4}+14\sqrt{2c_d}+14)MD/N$.
The $\omega$ term contributes at most
$28\sqrt{2c_d}M_2D/\sqrt T$, and
$q_{\rm ns}\ell_{\rm ns}^\Delta\le4M\ell_{\rm ns}^\Delta D/N$.
Combining these with the preceding vector bounds proves
\eqref{eq:corrupt-nonsmooth-explicit}.
Finally $B^{\rm rad}\ge T/(16N)$ and
$\Gamma=\max\{g,\Gamma_0\}\le g+d^{1/4}D/N$ prove
\eqref{eq:corrupt-floor-diagnostic-cost}.
For zero corruption, \eqref{eq:corrupt-bias-scales} gives exactly
$\beta=0$ and $\bar\sigma=\sigma_0$, so their additional terms vanish.

label: cor:corrupt-accuracy
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: A sufficient corruption allowance

title: Proof
body_md:
The legal-floor condition in \eqref{eq:corrupt-accuracy-common}
gives $g=64c_d\Delta D/\varepsilon\le\gamma_{\max}/2$.
The scalar corruption term is at most
$4\Delta(1+\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta)\le\varepsilon/16$.
For the nonsmooth floor, \eqref{eq:corrupt-accuracy-nonsmooth}
gives
\[
 \mu_dMg(1+\ell_{\rm ns}^\Delta)
 =\frac{64c_d\mu_dMD\Delta}{\varepsilon}
                                      (1+\ell_{\rm ns}^\Delta)
 \le\varepsilon/16.
\]
The smooth floor condition analogously gives
$\nu_dLg^2(1+\ell_{\rm s}^\Delta)\le\varepsilon/16$.
The direct bias and its curvature contribution obey
$(2+14/\sqrt N)\rho\le16\rho=\varepsilon/4$.
The additional vector variance is at most
$5c_{\rm vec}\kappa_d\rho/\sqrt T\le\varepsilon/16$ by
the first budget condition. Add these quantities to
$\mathcal C_{\mathrm{reg}}\le\varepsilon/2$: their sum is
$15\varepsilon/16<\varepsilon$. Zero corruption only removes terms.

label: lem:epsilon-clean-scales
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Clean coefficient and diagnostic scales

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $A=N(N+1)/2$. Both modes have
$B^{\rm rad}=\lfloor T/(8N)\rfloor\ge T/(16N)$ and
$c_{\rm vec}\le6$. Consequently,
\[
 \omega\le4M_2N/\sqrt T,
 \qquad \eta\le
 4d^{1/4}M_2D/(\sqrt N\sqrt T)\le4r_{\rm st}.
\]
Here $d\ge1$ and $N\ge1$ give
$d^{1/4}/\sqrt N\le\sqrt d$. Also $A/N^2\le1$.
Thus the vector term in $\mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}D^2/N^2$ is at most
$6\sigma_0D/\sqrt T$, and the smooth deterministic term is
$4r_{\rm s}$.

For the nonsmooth envelope, $\Gamma=\Gamma_0$ and
\[
 \Gamma^{-1}\le2/\gamma_{\max}+N/(d^{1/4}D),\qquad
 \sqrt{M(\mu_dM+\omega)}\le M+\omega/2.
\]
The first term in the nonsmooth envelope is therefore at most
$8a_{\rm ns}+4r_{\rm ns}$, because $c_d\le\sqrt d$.
Its square-root term is at most
\[
 2\sqrt2r_{\rm ns}
   +4\sqrt2d^{1/4}M_2D/\sqrt T
 \le2\sqrt2r_{\rm ns}+6\sqrt dM_2D/\sqrt T.
\]
The $2MN/D$ term contributes at most $2r_{\rm ns}$.
Together with the vector term these inequalities prove the two
coefficient bounds. Since $6+2\sqrt2<9$, their final simplifications
follow. Finally $A\ge N^2/2$ and $d^{1/4}\ge1$ give the two
$q_{\mathrm{reg}}$ bounds. All floor estimates hold already for $T\ge8N$;
the adaptive-batch branch retains its additional $T\ge16N$ condition.

label: thm:epsilon-clean
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Target-linked clean initialization

title: Proof
body_md:
At zero corruption the floor, bias and scalar corruption terms in
Theorem~\ref{thm:corrupt-radial} vanish. Its startup and reference
terms obey, because $R_u\le D$ and $2A\ge N^2$,
\[
 \frac{h_0R_u^2}{2A}+\frac{h_0D^2}{N^2}
 \le2\theta\varepsilon.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:epsilon-clean-scales} and
\eqref{eq:epsilon-initialization} give
$\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta\le\lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}^\varepsilon$. Also $k_N\le7/N^2$. Multiplying the
coefficient bounds of \eqref{eq:epsilon-clean-scales} by $k_NN^2\le7$,
adding $\eta(1+\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta)+q_{\mathrm{reg}}\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta$, and using their remaining
inequalities gives the displayed component bounds directly.
No new oracle observations are required for the initialization or
its interpretation, so all counts are unchanged.

label: cor:epsilon-clean-budgets
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Log-free sufficient clean budgets

title: Proof
body_md:
With $\theta=4/77$ and $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}\le\varepsilon/77$,
\eqref{eq:epsilon-calibrated-logs} gives
$\lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}^\varepsilon\le\log_2(13/4)<7/4$ in both branches. The last strict
inequality follows from $13^4=28561<32768=2^7\cdot4^4$.
The nonsmooth coefficients in
\eqref{eq:epsilon-clean-nonsmooth} are therefore bounded above by
$49+14\sqrt2$, $56$, and $53$. Since $\sqrt2<10/7$,
$49+14\sqrt2<69$. The corresponding smooth coefficients are at most
$63/2$ and $53$. The noninitial terms in either branch are strictly
less than $69\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}$ whenever $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}>0$.
Their sum with $2\theta\varepsilon=8\varepsilon/77$ is strictly
less than $\varepsilon$. If $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}=0$, the initial term alone
is at most $8\varepsilon/77<\varepsilon$.

In \eqref{eq:epsilon-explicit-smooth-budgets}, each of $r_{\rm s}$
and $r_{\rm st}$ is at most $\varepsilon/154$. In
\eqref{eq:epsilon-explicit-nonsmooth-budgets}, each of
$r_{\rm ns},a_{\rm ns},r_{\rm st}$ is at most $\varepsilon/231$.
This proves the sufficient conditions. Taking ceilings for integer
budgets, imposing $T\ge8N$ or $T\ge16N$, and using
$(\sigma_0+\sqrt dM_2)^2\le2(\sigma_0^2+dM_2^2)$ gives
\eqref{eq:epsilon-clean-complexities}.
