label: cor:epsilon-corruption-budgets
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Target-linked protected corruption budgets

label: eq:epsilon-corruption-envelope
title: Proof
body_md:
The finite-radius condition gives $g\le\gamma_{\max}/2$. For positive
$\Delta$, Corollary~\ref{cor:corrupt-bias-budget} gives
$D\beta\le\rho$ and
$\bar\sigma\le\sigma_0+\kappa_d\rho/D$.
Since $\Gamma\ge\Gamma_0$, the clean deterministic envelope bounds
of Lemma~\ref{lem:epsilon-clean-scales} remain valid. The additional
vector contributions give
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}D^2/N^2
 \le9\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}+
       \rho\left(\frac{c_{\rm vec}\kappa_d}{\sqrt T}
                       +\frac2{\sqrt N}\right).
 \label{eq:epsilon-corruption-envelope}
\end{equation}
Indeed, $A/N^2\le1$ bounds the added variance contribution,
and $\mathsf W_{N,2}\le N^3$ bounds the bias contribution.
The conditions on $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}},T$, and $N\ge1$ imply
\[
 \frac{\mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}D^2}{N^2}
 \le\varepsilon\left(\frac9{256}+
                  \frac1{64}\left(\frac45+2\right)\right)
 =\frac{101\varepsilon}{1280}.
\]
Dividing by $h_0D^2/N^2=4\varepsilon/77$ gives
$\mathcal H^\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}/h_0\le7777/5120$.
Since $1+7777/5120=12897/5120<8/3<2^{3/2}$, this proves
$\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta<3/2$. For $\Delta=0$ the same envelope bound holds with
its nonnegative additional term retained, so this conclusion is
also valid.

Write
$\eta_0=4d^{1/4}M_2D/(\sqrt N\sqrt T)\le4r_{\rm st}$ and
$\eta_g=4\sqrt{\nu_d}M_2g\sqrt{N/T}$.
Equation~\eqref{eq:corrupt-floor-diagnostic-cost} gives
$\eta\le\eta_0+\eta_g$.
Using $\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta<3/2$ in the exact component bounds from the clean
proof, the clean noninitial terms are at most
$68\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}$, strictly so when $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}>0$: in the
nonsmooth branch their coefficients are
at most $48+14\sqrt2<68$, $56$, and $52$, and in the smooth
branch they are at most $31$ and $52$. The initial and reference
terms remain at most $8\varepsilon/77$.

The additional vector bias and its curvature contribution are at
most $(2+14/\sqrt N)\rho\le\varepsilon/4$.
The added vector-variance contribution is at most
$5c_{\rm vec}\kappa_d\rho/\sqrt T\le\varepsilon/16$.
The scalar corruption contributes at most
$4\Delta(1+\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta)\le10\Delta\le\varepsilon/16$.
Each branch condition gives $w_{\mathrm{reg}}\le\varepsilon/40$, and hence
$w_{\mathrm{reg}}(1+\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^\Delta)\le\varepsilon/16$.
Finally the last budget condition in

name: Conditional fixed-radius geometry

title: Proof
body_md:
Condition on the complete anchor batch. Its realized $h_{\rm a}$,
$S$, $Q_S$ and $u_S$ are fixed, positive or finite as appropriate.
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:potential} and Lemma~\ref{lem:growth} to
$\phi$ itself, with zero comparator smoothing charge. The initial
potential is $h_{\rm a}\lVert u_S-x^0\rVert^2/2$, where
$\lVert u_S-x^0\rVert^2=\min\{R_u^2,S^2\}$.
Write $e_t^y=g_t^y-\nabla\phi(y_t)$, $e_t^x=g_t^x-\nabla\phi(x_t)$ and
$\mathcal E_N=\sum_tt^2\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert^2$.
The scalar coefficient bound is
$H_N-h_{\rm a}\le4L_\gamma+\sqrt{\mathcal E_N}/D_S$.
The fixed batch-size lower bounds satisfy
$B_t^\iota\ge T't/[2N(N+1)]$ for $\iota\in\{y,x\}$ because $T'\ge4N$.
The first mean is known before the second batch is drawn, so conditional
centering gives $\mathbb E[\langle e_t^x,e_t^y\rangle\mid\text{anchor}]=0$.
Thus $\mathbb E[\mathcal E_N\mid\text{anchor}]\le8\sigma_\gamma^2A^2/T'$.
The minimum adaptive batch sizes give instead $32\sigma_\gamma^2A^2/T'$.
Both error inner products in the potential have zero conditional
expectation, since their distance factors are known before the
corresponding batches are drawn. The remaining curvature contribution is
\[
 8L_\gamma D_S^2/A+
 2D_S\sqrt{\mathbb E[\mathcal E_N\mid\text{anchor}]}/A.
\]
Substitution of $D_S=2S$ proves \eqref{eq:frontier-conditional-risk}.
Compactness bounds the distance factors, and the positive reference
and scalar energy bound ensure integrability.

For the accounting with fixed batch sizes,
$2\sum_tB_t^y\le2N+2(T'-2N)\sum_tt/[N(N+1)]=T'$.
The added final labels spend the residual and preserve every floor.
There are two vector stages per optimizer step and one anchor stage.

$T'$. Each record contributes one pair and two values.

title: Theorem
head: environment
name: The cost of the relaxed affine error guarantee

label: eq:frontier-coupled-lower
title: Proof
body_md:
Since $h_{\rm ref}/A\le m/(p r_0)$ and $\Psi(R_0)\le5R_0^2/8$,
the deterministic-law error bound gives
\[
 \mathbb E_0(S-\widehat x)\le2\Psi(R_0)/(p r_0)
 \le5R_0^2/(4p r_0)=R_0/2.
\]
Thus $\mathbb E_0\widehat x\ge r_0(1+p/5)$.
Generate $n$ independent draws from the second law in advance,
including unused draws if the algorithm stops early. Couple its internal random seed across
the two instances. On the event that all draws select $F_0$,
the entire corresponding functions agree. Induction through the
adaptive transcript gives identical endpoints, batch allocations,
stopping decisions and output. This reasoning also permits repeated
evaluations under one label and full realized-function observation.
The event is independent of internal randomness and has probability
$q_n$. The rare gap is the nonnegative quantity
$m(1+1/n)\widehat x$. Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_1[f_1(\widehat x)-f_1(0)]
 \ge q_n m(1+1/n)r_0(1+p/5).
 \label{eq:frontier-coupled-lower}
\end{equation}

Since $\Psi(r_0)=r_0^2/2$, the deterministic terms in
\eqref{eq:frontier-local-contract} are at most
$m r_0(2+1/n)/(2p)$. Moreover
$\mathcal H_p(r_0)=(2+1/p)r_0$ and $\sigma_1\le2m\sqrt n$,
so its noise term is at most $2P m r_0(2+1/p)$.
Comparison with \eqref{eq:frontier-coupled-lower} proves
\eqref{eq:frontier-exact-lower}.

For completeness, let $g(x)=x\log(1-1/x)$ on $x\ge2$ and
$z=1/(x-1)$. Then
$g'(x)=z-\log(1+z)\ge0$, because
$\log(1+z)=\int_0^z(1+s)^{-1}\,ds\le z$.
Thus $q_n\ge\exp(g(2))=1/4$.
For $n\ge4$ the numerator of \eqref{eq:frontier-exact-lower}
is at least $1/4+p/20-9/(8p)$.
For $p\ge5$ its first and last terms have nonnegative sum,
and the denominator is at most $2(2+1/5)=22/5$.
Hence $P\ge(p/20)/(22/5)=p/88$.

label: lem:joint-offset-potential
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: The offset-controller potential

title: Proof
body_md:
Under the anchor law the geometry and initial coefficients are fixed.
Let $\mathsf S_N$ be the maximum positive radial mean normalized by its
trial radius. Conditional normalized means lie in $[0,M]$, and their
centered variances are at most $\chi_dM_2^2/B^{\rm rad}$.
Thus $\lVert \mathsf S_N\rVert_{L_2}\le M+\omega_{\rm rad}$ by bounding the squared
error maximum by the sum of squared errors and applying Minkowski.
No independence between iterations is required.

The reference satisfies $\underline K_t\le\mathsf K_{t-1}<2\underline K_t$.
Within a reference block, the reciprocal update is a maximum starting
from $\Gamma_S^{-1}$. Therefore
\begin{align}
 \gamma_t^{-1}&\le
 \max\{\Gamma_S^{-1},\mathsf S_NN^2/(\underline K_tD_S^2)\},\nonumber\\*
 L_t&\le\sqrt d M/\Gamma_S+
       2\sqrt dM\mathsf S_NN^2/(\mathsf K_{t-1}D_S^2).
 \label{eq:joint-reciprocal-control}
\end{align}
Fix a complete realization and define
\[
 \mathfrak K=4\sqrt dM/\Gamma_S+
             2\sqrt2d^{1/4}\sqrt{M\mathsf S_N}\,N/D_S.
\]
Write $a=\sqrt dM/\Gamma_S$ and
$b=\sqrt dM\mathsf S_NN^2/D_S^2$. Then
$\mathfrak K=4a+\sqrt{8b}$ and
$\mathfrak K^2-4a\mathfrak K-8b=4a\sqrt{8b}\ge0$.
Whenever $\mathsf K_{t-1}\ge\mathfrak K$,
\eqref{eq:joint-reciprocal-control} therefore gives
$4L_t\le4a+8b/\mathfrak K\le\mathfrak K$.
If $a=b=0$, every target is affine and the shifted-square argument
below applies directly with threshold zero.
Write $e_t^y=g_t^y-\nabla f_{\gamma_t}(y_t)$, $e_t^x=g_t^x-\nabla f_{\gamma_t}(x_t)$,
$\delta_t=H_t-H_{t-1}$ and
$\mathcal E_N=\sum_tt^2\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert^2$.
The scalar balance and secant bound give
\begin{align*}
 \delta_tD_S^2
 &\le[-(H_t-4L_t)r_t^2/2+t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert r_t]_+\\
 &\le[-(\mathsf K_t-\mathfrak K)r_t^2/2
                   +t\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert r_t]_+.
\end{align*}
Here $H_t\ge\mathsf K_t$ is essential.
Because $\mathsf K_t-\mathsf K_{t-1}=\delta_t$, completion of
a square gives the positive-part square recurrence after this crossing.
Before it, the gradient-norm envelope and $r_t\le D_S$ give
$\delta_t\le t(2M+\lVert e_t^x-e_t^y\rVert)/D_S$.
There is at most one crossing. Its noisy jump and all later energy
combine using $\sqrt{(a+\sqrt q)^2+b}\le a+\sqrt{q+b}$.
Consequently
\[
 H_N-h_{\rm a}=\mathsf K_N-h_{\rm ref}
 \le\mathfrak K+2NM/D_S+\sqrt{\mathcal E_N}/D_S.
\]
If $h_{\rm ref}\ge\mathfrak K$, the square recurrence holds throughout
and gives a stronger bound.
The lower bounds on the vector batch sizes yield
$\sqrt{\mathbb E[\mathcal E_N\mid\text{anchor}]}\le
c_{\rm vec}\sigma_0A/\sqrt{T'}$.
Also $\mathbb E\sqrt{M\mathsf S_N}\le M+\omega_{\rm rad}/2$.
Thus the conditional expected coefficient increase is bounded by
$\mathcal H_{{\rm j},\rm ns}(D_S)$.
Under smoothness, Lemma~\ref{lem:growth} instead gives
$\mathcal H_{{\rm j},\rm s}(D_S)$.

Each nonzero replacement at least doubles the reference. If $J$ is
their number, then
\[
 J\le\log_2(\mathsf K_N/h_{\rm ref}),\qquad
 \sum_{t:I_t=1}\underline K_t\le2(\mathsf K_N-h_{\rm ref})=2(H_N-h_{\rm a}).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:radial-affine} bounds the selected local charge,
conditionally on the history preceding its diagnostic, by
$\underline K_tD_S^2/N^2+\eta(D_S)$ in expectation.
Its weighted average is at most
$D_S^2\mathbb E[\mathsf K_N\mid\text{anchor}]/N^2+\eta(D_S)$.
At a reexpansion event the positive target drift is at most this new
local charge plus the Bregman remainder at $(x_{t-1},y_t)$.
Since $\lVert x_{t-1}-y_t\rVert\le2D_S/(t+1)$, the weighted remainder
is at most $2MD_SN$, or $LD_S^2$ under smoothness.
The event is known before its radial stage, so its charge may be averaged
conditionally first. The expected radial drift is at most
$2D_S^2\mathbb E[H_N-h_{\rm a}\mid\text{anchor}]/N^2
+\eta(D_S)\mathbb E[J\mid\text{anchor}]$.

Theorem~\ref{thm:radial-potential} retains this positive target drift
and charges $2D_S^2\mathbb E[H_N-h_{\rm a}\mid\text{anchor}]/A$ for
scalar growth. Combining the preceding terms gives
\eqref{eq:joint-conditional-risk}, after Jensen bounds the event count
by $\ell(D_S)$. Every diagnostic error is averaged at its predictable
event; no product with a future random logarithm is bounded directly.
The moment estimates also ensure integrability.

For adaptive-batch accounting, $T'\ge16N$ gives the original floors and
$\mathsf U\ge5T'/8$. For the accounting with fixed batch sizes, $T'\ge8N$ gives
$B^{\rm rad}\ge T'/(16N)$ and
$\mathsf U_{\rm pub}\ge7T'/8\ge7N\ge4N$.
Its floors yield energy at most $64\sigma_0^2A^2/(7T')$.
Allocating the remaining samples and including the initial batch proves
all stated counts.

label: lem:run5-distance-moment
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Anchor-radius second moment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $a=r_0$, $b=2p r_0$, $k=\kappa$ and
$F(w)=[a+b\sqrt w/(k+\sqrt w)]^2$ for $w\ge0$. It is increasing,
bounded and continuous at zero. At $z=\sqrt w>0$,
\[
 F''(w)=-\frac{bk[3(a+b)z+4ak+ak^2/z]}{2z^2(k+z)^4}<0.
\]
Indeed, writing $s(z)=a+bz/(k+z)$, differentiation gives
$F''=[(s')^2+ss''-ss'/z]/(2z^2)$,
$s'=bk/(k+z)^2$ and $s''=-2bk/(k+z)^3$.
After factoring $bk/(k+z)^4$, the numerator is
$bk-s(k+z)(3+k/z)=-3(a+b)z-4ak-ak^2/z$.
Continuity extends concavity to $[0,\infty)$. Centering gives
$\mathbb E\lVert g_0\rVert^2=G_{\rm a}^2+
\mathbb E\lVert g_0-\nabla f_{\gamma_{\rm a}}(x^0)\rVert^2\le z_{\rm a}^2$.
Jensen and monotonicity therefore yield
$\mathbb E S^2=\mathbb E F(\lVert g_0\rVert^2)\le F(z_{\rm a}^2)=S_2^2$.
Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\mathbb E S\le S_2$. If $z_{\rm a}=0$, then
$g_0=0$ almost surely and $S=r_0$. The strict upper bound follows
from $\kappa>0$ and finite $z_{\rm a}$.

label: lem:run5-distance-clipping
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Saturated startup and clipping price

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\phi=f_{\gamma_{\rm a}}$, $z=\lVert g_0\rVert$ and
$e_0=g_0-\nabla\phi(x^0)$. If $R_u>S$, set $\theta=S/R_u$.
Segment convexity and the tangent inequality at $x^0$ give
\[
 \phi(u_S)-\phi(u)
 \le(1-\theta)[\phi(x^0)-\phi(u)]\le G_{\rm a}(R_u-S).
\]
If $R_u\le S$, the difference is zero. Thus
$\phi(u_S)-f(u)\le G_{\rm a}(R_u-S)_++\beta_{\rm a}(u)$.
Since $|G_{\rm a}-z|\le\lVert e_0\rVert$ and
$S=r_0+(2A/h_{\rm a})z$,
\[
 G_{\rm a}(R_u-S)_+\le
 z[a_{R_u}-(2A/h_{\rm a})z]_++a_{R_u}\lVert e_0\rVert
 \le\frac{h_{\rm a}a_{R_u}^2}{8A}+a_{R_u}\lVert e_0\rVert.
\]
The last inequality maximizes $z(a_{R_u}-cz)$ with $c=2A/h_{\rm a}$;
it holds for every realized positive $h_{\rm a}$.
Bounding the startup distance by $R_u$ gives the charge
$h_{\rm a}\Psi(R_u)/A+a_{R_u}\lVert e_0\rVert+\beta_{\rm a}(u)$.
The inequalities $\mathbb E z\le G_{\rm a}+\sigma_{\rm a}/\sqrt{B_0}$ and
$\mathbb E\lVert e_0\rVert\le\sigma_{\rm a}/\sqrt{B_0}$ prove
\eqref{eq:run5-distance-old-price}.

For the other price retain
$V=\lVert u_S-x^0\rVert^2=\min\{R_u^2,S^2\}$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:run5-distance-moment} gives
$\mathbb E V\le\min\{R_u^2,S_2^2\}$. Pointwise $V^2\le R_u^4$ and
$V^2\le S^4\le r_p^2S^2$, so
$\mathbb E V^2\le\min\{R_u^4,r_p^2S_2^2\}$.
Cauchy--Schwarz consequently gives
\[
 \mathbb E[zV]\le\sqrt{\mathbb E z^2\,\mathbb E V^2}
       \le z_{\rm a}\min\{R_u^2,r_p S_2\}.
\]
Expand $h_{\rm a}$ and use $S\ge r_0$ in the clipping term to obtain
\eqref{eq:run5-distance-saturated-price}. Both prices bound the same
expected charge, so their minimum applies. The original-function
version follows from $f(u_S)\le\phi(u_S)$. The fourth power here is
that of the bounded radius; no fourth anchor moment is assumed.

sum of the startup and comparator charges by $\mathcal A_*(u)$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:run5-distance-moment} gives $\mathbb E S^2\le S_2^2$ and
$\mathbb E S\le S_2$, proving \eqref{eq:run5-distance-fixed-risk}.
The allocation is unchanged: the anchor and two stages with fixed batch sizes or four with adaptive
batch sizes per optimization iteration use all $T$ sampled functions, with two values for each
sampled function and one intersection projection per iteration. The required budgets
ensure $T'\ge4N$ or $8N$, respectively, as used in the conditional lemma.
head: environment

label: thm:run5-distance-joint
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Joint anchor moment refinement

title: Proof
body_md:
Conditional on the full anchor, Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-offset-potential}
gives the startup charge plus $\mathcal U_{\mathrm{reg}}(D_S,\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(D_S))$, where
$\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(D)=\log_2(1+\mathcal H_{\mathrm{reg}}(D)/h_{\rm ref})$.
Add clipping and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:run5-distance-clipping}, in its
original-function version. Since $D_S\ge2r_0$ and $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{reg}}$ is
decreasing, $\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(D_S)\le\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}^0$. Its coefficients are nonnegative;
replace the logarithm by this deterministic bound before averaging.

For the smooth envelope, $D^2\mathcal H_{\rm s}(D)=4LD^2+vD$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:run5-distance-moment} gives
$\mathbb E D_S^2\le4S_2^2$ and $\mathbb E D_S\le2S_2$.
The reference and smooth target-drift terms are multiples of $D^2$.
The function $\eta(D)$ is increasing and concave, as a positive
multiple of the minimum of a constant and a linear map. Jensen gives
$\mathbb E\eta(D_S)\le\eta(\mathbb E D_S)\le\eta(2S_2)$.
These substitutions prove \eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-smooth}.

Under the untruncated-evaluation domain condition, every anchor outcome has
$\Gamma(D_S)=d^{1/4}D_S/N$. Thus
$D^2\mathcal H_{\rm ns}(D)=(4d^{1/4}MN+C_{\rm ns})D$,
and this term, $q_{\rm ns}$ and $\eta$ are linear on the whole observed
range. Their first moments and the reference term's second moment
give \eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-nonsmooth}.

For an arbitrary finite evaluation domain, pointwise
\[
 \frac{D^2}{\Gamma(D)}
 =\max\left\{\frac{D^2}{\gamma_{\max}},\frac{ND}{d^{1/4}}\right\}
 \le\frac{D^2}{\gamma_{\max}}+\frac{ND}{d^{1/4}}.
\]
Use both radius moments here and in the other linear and quadratic
terms, and use concavity for $\eta$. The result is exactly
$\mathcal V_{\rm ns}(S_2,\ell_{\rm ns}^0)$.
Independently, $D_S\le2r_p$ and monotonicity of each cost factor at
fixed logarithm give $\mathcal U_{\rm ns}(2r_p,\ell_{\rm ns}^0)$.
Each cost bound can be combined with either anchor-price bound,
because they bound separate expected charges. Taking both minima
proves \eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-finite-halo}.
All algorithmic stages and allocation rules remain those of the
joint controller, including the anchor and each three-stage iteration with fixed batch sizes
or five-stage iteration with adaptive batch sizes.
head: environment

label: cor:run5-distance-stationary
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Original stationary distance

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $U$ be uniform on the unit ball. Smoothness permits differentiation
under the bounded ball integral. Jensen, original stationarity and
gradient Lipschitz continuity give
\begin{align*}
 G_{\rm a}^2
 &=\lVert \mathbb E_U\nabla f(x^0+\gamma_{\rm a}U)\rVert^2\\
 &\le\mathbb E_U\lVert \nabla f(x^0+\gamma_{\rm a}U)-\nabla f(u)\rVert^2\\
 &\le L^2\mathbb E_U\lVert x^0-u+\gamma_{\rm a}U\rVert^2
 =L^2(R_u^2+\nu_d\gamma_{\rm a}^2).
\end{align*}
Here $\mathbb E U=0$ and $\mathbb E\lVert U\rVert^2=\nu_d$.
Ball averaging of the smooth upper model at $u$ yields
$\beta_{\rm a}(u)\le L\nu_d\gamma_{\rm a}^2/2$.
Both prices are increasing in the nonnegative quantities
$G_{\rm a},z_{\rm a},S_2,\beta_{\rm a}(u)$, and the smooth cost at a
fixed nonnegative logarithm is increasing in $D$. Substitution into
\eqref{eq:run5-distance-joint-smooth} proves the result.
If the gradient is affine, symmetry gives
$\nabla f_{\gamma_{\rm a}}(x^0)=\nabla f(x^0)$, and original
stationarity yields $G_{\rm a}\le LR_u$. No distance to a smoothed
minimizer is assumed.
head: environment

label: cor:run5-distance-reference-absorption
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Absorbing a reference chosen before sampling

title: Proof
body_md:
Theorem~\ref{thm:run5-distance-joint} permits the saturated price instead
of its minimum with $\mathcal A_p(u)$. Its explicit startup reference
term satisfies
\[
 \frac{h_{\rm ref}\min\{R_u^2,S_2^2\}}{2A}
 \le\frac{h_{\rm ref}r_p^2}{N^2},
\]
because $S_2\le r_p$ and $2A=N(N+1)\ge N^2$.
In the smooth or untruncated nonsmooth cost, the other explicit
reference term is $4h_{\rm ref}S_2^2/N^2$, at most
$4h_{\rm ref}r_p^2/N^2$.
For a finite nonsmooth evaluation domain, the two candidate geometry bounds have
reference terms $4h_{\rm ref}r_p^2/N^2$ and
$4h_{\rm ref}S_2^2/N^2$. Both are bounded by the former.
For any real $b_1,b_2$ and $q_1,q_2\le q$,
$\min\{b_1+q_1,b_2+q_2\}\le\min\{b_1,b_2\}+q$.
Apply this identity to the finite-radius minimum. In every regime the
remaining geometry cost is bounded by
$\mathcal J_{\mathrm{reg}}^0(S_2)+4h_{\rm ref}r_p^2/N^2$.
Adding the startup bound proves
\eqref{eq:run5-distance-absorbed-risk}.
Finally $r_p=r_0(1+2p)$ depends only on inputs chosen before sampling, so the specified
positive reference choice makes its displayed polynomial charge at
most $\varepsilon/4$ without knowledge of the problem scales.
head: environment

label: prop:run5-distance-curved
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: An exact curved trajectory

title: Proof
body_md:
In one dimension, for either $e\in\{-1,1\}$ and every radius,
\[
 \frac{f_L(z+\gamma e)-f_L(z-\gamma e)}{2\gamma}e=L(z-R).
\]
All vector means are exact. The anchor is $-G$ and selects
$h_{\rm a}=h$ and the displayed $S$. The first projected vector is
$q\in Q$, with $x_1=q$. For $D_S=2S$ its post coefficient is
\[
 H_1=h+\kappa_q(L-h/2),\qquad
 \kappa_q=\frac{q^2}{D_S^2+q^2/2}<\frac1{16A^2}\le\frac1{16}.
\]
The second center is $y_2=q$. Its tentative vector
$q-2(Lq-G)/H_1$ is nonpositive when
$(2-\kappa_q)L\ge(3-\kappa_q/2)h$.
The assumption $L\ge2Ah\ge2h$ suffices because
$2(2-\kappa_q)-(3-\kappa_q/2)=1-3\kappa_q/2>0$.
Thus $v_2=0$, $x_2=q/A_2$. If the claim holds at $t-1\ge2$, then
$y_t=q/A_t\ge q/A\ge2G/L=2R$, so its gradient is positive.
From $v_{t-1}=0$ projection sends the tentative negative point to zero,
and averaging gives $x_t=q/A_t$. This proves the trajectory by
induction; for $N=1$ the first step alone suffices. Since
$R\le q/(2A)$, the risk bound follows.

Every selected-radius vector gradient is identical in the joint
controller. Its projected vectors, averaged iterates, scalar inner
products and post coefficients are consequently identical; radial
stages change only radii and references. A deterministic sample
Lipschitz envelope on an open neighborhood of the finite evaluation domain is
$M_{2,L}=L(S+\gamma_{\max}+r_0)+G$. This supplies all radial moments at
legal radii. Independent draws from this point-mass distribution satisfy the two-value
same-sample oracle model.
head: environment

label: cor:run5-distance-curved-transfer
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Failure of comparator-only curvature transfer

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $R\le r_0$, $\Psi(R)=R^2/2$, and the first two proposed charges
sum to $hR^2/(2A)$. Quadratic ball smoothing in dimension one gives
$\beta_\gamma(u)=L\gamma^2/6\le Lq^2/(24A^2)$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:run5-distance-curved} therefore gives
\[
 f_L(x_N)-f_L(u)-\beta_\gamma(u)\ge\frac{Lq^2}{12A^2}.
\]
The remaining proposed right side is
$hG^2/(2AL^2)+CG^2/(AL)+E_0$, which remains bounded as $L\to\infty$.
The left side diverges. A fixed logarithmic polynomial times $1/L$
still tends to zero, proving the last assertion.
head: environment

label: lem:prestep-relative-moments
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:prestep-relative-moments}
Suppose the population expectations exist at the queried points.
Assume the weak-gradient, segment-integrability and uniform
sample-gradient second-moment bound with envelope $M_2^2$ on the
evaluation domain, or a random sample Lipschitz envelope with second
moment at most $M_2^2$. Then, at every fixed $x,y\in Q$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E P_\gamma(x,y)=\phi(x)-\phi(y),\qquad
 \mathbb E P_\gamma(x,y)^2\le M_2^2\lVert x-y\rVert^2.
 \label{eq:prestep-value-moments}
\end{equation}
\nopagebreak[4]
An average of $B^q$ conditionally independent records consequently has
centered conditional variance at most
$M_2^2\lVert x-y\rVert^2/B^q$.
head: environment
name: Relative-function moments

title: Proof
body_md:
Taking expectations of the same sampled function at both endpoints, followed by the
ball average, gives the mean. Under the gradient assumptions, the
fundamental theorem along the shifted segment gives
\[
 P_\gamma(x,y)=\int_0^1
 \langle \nabla F(y+\gamma U+s(x-y),\xi),x-y\rangle\,ds
\]
almost surely. The shifted segment remains in the convex evaluation
domain. Jensen and Cauchy--Schwarz give a bound by
$\lVert x-y\rVert^2\int_0^1
\lVert \nabla F(y+\gamma U+s(x-y),\xi)\rVert^2ds$
for the squared record. The segment-integrability assumption permits
Fubini and yields the claimed second moment. At a largest legal
boundary radius, sample continuity and increasing inner radii yield
the same bound by Fatou; uniform second moments give uniform
integrability for the mean. Under the alternative Lipschitz assumption,
the pointwise inequality
$|P_\gamma(x,y)|\le m(\xi)\lVert x-y\rVert$ proves the bound directly.
Conditional independence and centering of the $B^q$ records divide their
variance by $B^q$.
head: environment

label: thm:prestep-potential
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Original-comparator accepted-trial potential

title: Proof
body_md:
Projection optimality gives, at any trial,
\[
 a_j\langle g_j,v_j^+-u\rangle
 \le\frac{h_0}{2}\left(
 \lVert u-v^-\rVert^2-\lVert u-v_j^+\rVert^2-\lVert w_j\rVert^2\right).
\]
The center identity and convexity at $y_j$ give
\[
 A^-\phi(x^-)+a_j\phi(u)
 \ge A_j^+\phi(y_j)
             +a_j\langle \nabla\phi(y_j),u-v^-\rangle.
\]
Also $A_j^+(x_j^+-y_j)=a_jw_j$. Combining these identities, writing
$\nabla\phi(y_j)=g_j-e_j$, and adding the distance potential yields
\begin{align*}
 &A_j^+[\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(u)]
                    +\frac{h_0}{2}\lVert u-v_j^+\rVert^2\\
 &\quad\le A^-[\phi(x^-)-\phi(u)]
                    +\frac{h_0}{2}\lVert u-v^-\rVert^2\\
 &\qquad\quad+
 A_j^+\bigl[\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(y_j)
                       -\langle g_j,x_j^+-y_j\rangle\bigr]
       -\frac{h_0}{2}\lVert w_j\rVert^2
       +a_j\langle e_j,u-v^-\rangle.
\end{align*}
On an accepted trial, substitute the observed model inequality
\eqref{eq:prestep-acceptance} and
$\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(y_j)=\widehat q_j-\zeta_j^q$.
The last three terms are bounded by $\chi_j+Z_j(u)$.
Rejected trials do not change the accepted state. Summing only the
accepted transitions, using $A_0=0$, proves
\eqref{eq:prestep-pathwise-potential}. Finally,
$f(x_n)-f(u)\le\phi(x_n)-\phi(u)+\beta_\gamma(u)$ proves
\eqref{eq:prestep-original-potential}. At $n=0$ the potential is its
initial value and both claims hold as equalities or inequalities
directly.
head: environment

label: prop:prestep-rejection-charge
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:prestep-rejection-charge}
Suppose $Q$ is compact, $\phi$ is continuously differentiable on $Q$,
$K_{\rm tr}<\infty$, and all vector means and relative-value means
satisfy uniform finite conditional second-moment envelopes under
the histories preceding their respective batches. Assume their conditional means are respectively
$\nabla\phi(y_j)$ and $\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(y_j)$.
The curvature candidate is nondecreasing and at least
$\mathcal L_0>0$. Suppose additionally that the nonnegative
allowances have integrable total. Then all potential and error terms
below are integrable, and
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E\left[A_n[\phi(x_n)-\phi(u)]
                  +\frac{h_0}{2}\lVert u-v_n\rVert^2\right]
 \le{}&\frac{h_0}{2}R_u^2
        +\mathbb E\sum_{j\in\mathcal A}\chi_j
        -\mathbb E\sum_{j\in\mathcal R}Z_j(u).
 \label{eq:prestep-rejection-expectation}
\end{align}
This is a weighted guarantee with a random terminal $A_n$.
The rejected-error term records the dependence introduced by model
selection.
head: environment
name: Expected error from rejected trials

title: Proof
body_md:
We first justify integrability under a uniform second-moment
envelope, as in the stated oracle assumptions. Let
$c=h_0/\mathcal L_0$. From \eqref{eq:prestep-weight},
$a_j\le c+\sqrt{cA^-}$. By induction on the number $t$ of accepted
states, $A_t\le c(t+1)^2$: the bound at $t=0$ is immediate, and
$A_{t+1}\le c[(t+1)^2+(t+1)+1]\le c(t+2)^2$.
Thus every executed candidate has
$a_j\le c(K_{\rm tr}+2)$ and
$A_j^+\le c(K_{\rm tr}+2)^2$.
The accepted and tentative points belong to the compact set $Q$;
$\phi$ and all distances are bounded there. Uniform conditional
second moments, these weight bounds and the finite trial cap make
every $Z_j(u)$ integrable.

The execution indicator of each trial, its weight, first center and
$u-v^-$ are known before its vector samples are drawn. Therefore the
expectation of its first error inner product is zero. Its tentative
second center and $A_j^+$ are known before the function-difference samples are drawn, so the expectation of the second error term is zero separately.
Summing over the at most $K_{\rm tr}$ executed trials gives
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_{j\in\mathcal A\cup\mathcal R}Z_j(u)=0.
\]
No accepted or rejected indicator was included in these separate
centering steps. Since their sums partition every executed trial,
$\mathbb E\sum_{\mathcal A}Z_j=-\mathbb E\sum_{\mathcal R}Z_j$.
Taking expectations of \eqref{eq:prestep-pathwise-potential} proves
\eqref{eq:prestep-rejection-expectation}.
head: environment

label: thm:prestep-exact-distance
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:prestep-exact-distance}
Suppose $\phi$ is convex and $L$-smooth on $Q$, each $g_j$ equals
$\nabla\phi(y_j)$, each $\widehat q_j$ equals
$\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(y_j)$, and $\chi_j=0$.
Let the first curvature candidate be $\mathcal L_0$ and carry it
across successes, doubling it only on rejections. Define
\[
 J_\star=\left\lceil
       \log_2\max\{1,L/\mathcal L_0\}\right\rceil,\qquad
 \overline{\mathcal L}=\max\{\mathcal L_0,2L\}.
\]
A trial cap $K_{\rm tr}\ge N+J_\star$ guarantees $N$ acceptances.
There are at most $J_\star$ rejected trials, every curvature
candidate is at most $\overline{\mathcal L}$, and
\begin{equation}
 A_N\ge\frac{h_0N^2}{4\overline{\mathcal L}},\qquad
 \phi(x_N)-\phi(u)
 \le\frac{h_0R_u^2}{2A_N}
 \le\frac{2\overline{\mathcal L}R_u^2}{N^2}
 \label{eq:prestep-exact-rate}
\end{equation}
for every fixed $u\in Q$. The coefficient and the accepted trajectory
persist throughout. Each rejected trial has the full pair, stage and
projection costs stated in the execution.
head: environment
name: Exact-record scalar backtracking

title: Proof
body_md:
Smoothness and the center identity give
\begin{align*}
 A_j^+\bigl[\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(y_j)
             -\langle \nabla\phi(y_j),x_j^+-y_j\rangle\bigr]
 &\le \frac{LA_j^+}{2}\lVert x_j^+-y_j\rVert^2\\*
 &=\frac{La_j^2}{2A_j^+}\lVert w_j\rVert^2
 =\frac{h_0L}{2\mathcal L_j}\lVert w_j\rVert^2.
\end{align*}
Every candidate $\mathcal L_j\ge L$ therefore passes. Each rejection
must occur below $L$, so its doubling yields a candidate below $2L$.
Monotonicity of the candidate then proves the uniform bound and the
total rejection count. In particular, $N+J_\star$ trials suffice.

For an accepted weight,
$a_t=\sqrt{h_0A_t/\mathcal L_t}$ and $A_t=A_{t-1}+a_t$.
Consequently,
\[
 \sqrt{A_t}-\sqrt{A_{t-1}}
 =\frac{a_t}{\sqrt{A_t}+\sqrt{A_{t-1}}}
 \ge\frac12\sqrt{h_0/\mathcal L_t}
 \ge\frac12\sqrt{h_0/\overline{\mathcal L}}.
\]
Sum from $A_0=0$ to obtain the lower bound on $A_N$.
All retained errors and allowances vanish in
\eqref{eq:prestep-pathwise-potential}. Discarding its nonnegative
terminal distance and dividing by $A_N>0$ proves the risk bounds.
head: environment

label: thm:prestep-rare-curvature
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:prestep-rare-curvature}
Fix $D,G,\gamma_{\max}>0$ and a positive integer pair budget $T$.
Let $Q=[0,D]$, $x^0=0$, and let an arbitrary randomized adaptive
algorithm draw at most $T$ independent sampled functions, each evaluated at exactly two
endpoints in $[-\gamma_{\max},D+\gamma_{\max}]$, and return a point in $Q$.
All samples from rejected trials, pilot batches and diagnostics are included in this
budget. The algorithm receives no supplied population smoothness,
sample regularity, variance or original-distance parameter.
Its other supplied inputs are held fixed.

For the deterministic sample function $F_0(x)=-Gx$, let $W\in Q$
be its output and suppose $w=(\mathbb E W^2)^{1/2}>0$.
For every $L\ge\max\{G/D,2G/w\}$ put
\begin{equation}
 p=\frac1{4T},\qquad
 F_L(x,\xi)=-Gx+\frac{L\xi}{2p}x^2,\qquad
 \xi\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p).
 \label{eq:prestep-rare-sample}
\end{equation}
This oracle has a convex globally $L$-smooth population
$f_L(x)=-Gx+Lx^2/2$ with original stationary minimizer
$x^\star=R=G/L\in Q$. Its samples are convex and have finite
second moments on the entire evaluation domain. For the standard
one-dimensional symmetric vector record, uniform center variance
and sample regularity envelopes may be taken as
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_0=LD\sqrt{\frac{1-p}{p}},\qquad
 M_2=G+\frac{L(D+\gamma_{\max})}{\sqrt p}.
 \label{eq:prestep-rare-moments}
\end{equation}
Nevertheless the output $X_L$ obeys
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E[f_L(X_L)-f_L(x^\star)]
 &\ge\frac{3Lw^2}{32},\nonumber\\
 \frac{\sigma_0R}{\sqrt T}&\le2GD,\qquad
 \frac{M_2R}{\sqrt T}
 \le\frac{G^2}{L\sqrt T}+2G(D+\gamma_{\max}).
 \label{eq:prestep-rare-risk}
\end{align}
The statement allows arbitrary nonsymmetric pairs and adaptive
endpoint locations. It imposes no restriction on the optimizer
states, restarts or sequential sampling stages.
head: environment
name: A rare-curvature original-distance obstruction

title: Proof
body_md:
The population mean and its minimizer follow directly from
$\mathbb E\xi=p$. Completing the square gives
$f_L(x)-f_L(x^\star)=L(x-G/L)^2/2$.
The lower bound on $L$ places the stationary minimizer inside $Q$.

Each sample is a convex polynomial. Put $b=D+\gamma_{\max}$.
Its derivative is $-G+L\xi x/p$.
On the evaluation domain, a sample Lipschitz envelope is
$m(\xi)=G+Lb\xi/p$ and Minkowski gives
$(\mathbb E m(\xi)^2)^{1/2}\le G+Lb/\sqrt p$.
Thus the displayed $M_2$ is a valid uniform sample-gradient and
sample-Lipschitz second-moment envelope. The same envelope holds on
an open neighborhood of the evaluation domain. Indeed, choose
$0<\eta_{\rm dom}\le\min\{D/2,Gp/L\}$. On
$(-\gamma_{\max}-\eta_{\rm dom},b+\eta_{\rm dom})$, the rare sample
has derivative supremum
$L(b+\eta_{\rm dom})/p-G$: its positive endpoint dominates the
negative endpoint because $LD/p-2G\ge2G$. The squared second moment
of this supremum, including the common sample, is
\[
 G^2-2GL(b+\eta_{\rm dom})
       +\frac{L^2(b+\eta_{\rm dom})^2}{p}.
\]
Subtracting it from $(G+Lb/\sqrt p)^2$ and using
$L\eta_{\rm dom}\le Gp$ gives a difference at least
$2GLb/\sqrt p+GL\eta_{\rm dom}>0$.
Each function value also has a finite second moment throughout
this bounded neighborhood. In dimension one the symmetric vector
record at any legal radius is exactly
$-G+L\xi z/p$ at center $z$, because the quadratic central
difference equals its derivative. Its centered variance is
$L^2z^2(1-p)/p\le L^2D^2(1-p)/p$.
This proves all moment assumptions without restricting the radius.

Couple the algorithm's internal random seed with its deterministic
execution on $F_0$. Draw $T$ independent Bernoulli variables in
advance, using them in order as sampled functions are requested.
Let $E$ be the event that they are all zero. It is independent of the
algorithm seed and has probability
$(1-p)^T\ge1-Tp=3/4$.
On $E$, every sampled loss function equals
$F_0$ at every point. Induction through every adaptive query and
internal decision shows that both values, both endpoint locations,
the stopping decision and the output have the deterministic-oracle
transcript. This argument also covers any samples unused by an early
stop. In particular, on $E$, $X_L=W$ under the common seed.

Since the loss gap is nonnegative everywhere,
\[
 \mathbb E[f_L(X_L)-f_L(x^\star)]
 \ge\frac{3L}{8}\mathbb E(W-R)^2.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\mathbb E W\le w$, so
$\mathbb E(W-R)^2=w^2-2R\mathbb E W+R^2\ge(w-R)^2$.
The assumption $L\ge2G/w$ implies $R\le w/2$, proving the
first risk inequality. Finally $pT=1/4$ and $R=G/L$ give
\[
 \frac{\sigma_0R}{\sqrt T}
 =GD\sqrt{\frac{1-p}{pT}}\le2GD,\qquad
 \frac{M_2R}{\sqrt T}
 =\frac{G^2}{L\sqrt T}+\frac{Gb}{\sqrt{pT}},
\]
which proves the remaining bounds.
head: environment

label: cor:prestep-rare-price
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: A necessary additional adaptation price

title: Proof
body_md:
Equation~\eqref{eq:prestep-rare-moments} gives
$\sigma_0D/\sqrt T=LD^2\sqrt{4-1/T}\le2LD^2$.
Substitute this bound into the first inequality of
\eqref{eq:prestep-rare-risk}, proving
\eqref{eq:prestep-rare-diameter-price}.
For the linear-progress condition,
$G(D-\mathbb E W)\le GD/2$ implies $\mathbb E W\ge D/2$;
thus $w^2\ge(\mathbb E W)^2\ge D^2/4$.

In \eqref{eq:prestep-pure-distance-template},
$(L+h_0)R^2/N^2=G^2/(LN^2)+h_0G^2/(L^2N^2)$ tends to zero
as $L$ grows, and both statistical products remain bounded by
\eqref{eq:prestep-rare-risk}. Its right side is therefore bounded
for fixed supplied inputs, whereas the lower bound grows linearly in
$L$. This is a contradiction for sufficiently large $L$.
Along this family $\sigma_0,M_2,R^{-1}$ all grow at most linearly
in $L$, and every fixed product of their logarithmic powers grows
more slowly than $L$. The same contradiction applies.
head: environment

label: lem:preconf-robust-means
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:preconf-robust-means}
For positive error tolerances, suppose the vector observations are independent
conditional on the preceding history, with common mean
$\mu$ and centered second moment at most $\bar\sigma^2$ at the
center determined by that history. If each of $k$ odd blocks has at least
$72\bar\sigma^2/\eta_g^2$ records, the selected vector above
satisfies
\[
 \Pr\{\lVert g-\mu\rVert>\eta_g\mid\text{preceding history}\}
 \le2^{-k/2}.
 \label{eq:preconf-vector-confidence}
\]
Under the same conditional independence assumption, suppose scalar
observations have conditional mean $q$ and
centered variance at most $\overline M_2^2s^2$, with $s\ge0$ known
before these observations. If each block has at least
$8\overline M_2^2/\eta_q^2$ records, their median satisfies
\[
 \Pr\{|\widehat q-q|>\eta_qs\mid\text{preceding history}\}
 \le2^{-k/2}.
 \label{eq:preconf-scalar-confidence}
\]
The vector and scalar aggregates need not be unbiased.
head: environment
name: Robust records under finite second moments

title: Proof
body_md:
For a vector block mean $\bar z$ of size $b$, independence and
centering give $\mathbb E\lVert \bar z-\mu\rVert^2\le\bar\sigma^2/b$.
With $r=\eta_g/3$, Chebyshev's inequality therefore bounds the
probability of $\lVert \bar z-\mu\rVert>r$ by $1/8$.
If a strict majority of the block means lie within $r$ of $\mu$,
any one of these good blocks has median distance at most $2r$.
The selected block thus has at least $(k+1)/2$ blocks within $2r$.
This set intersects the good majority, so the triangle inequality
places the selected block within $3r=\eta_g$ of $\mu$.
Failure requires at least $(k+1)/2\ge k/2$ bad blocks.
Independence and a union bound over subsets give
$2^k(1/8)^{k/2}=2^{-k/2}$.

For scalar blocks and $s>0$, Chebyshev with radius $\eta_qs$ gives
the same $1/8$ bound. A good majority forces the scalar median
inside $[q-\eta_qs,q+\eta_qs]$. The same subset argument applies.
For $s=0$, variance zero makes every scalar observation equal to
its mean almost surely, so the conclusion holds directly.
All arguments are conditional on the history fixing the center,
scale and block size.

label: lem:preconf-weight-account
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Sum of the executed trial weights

title: Proof
body_md:
For an accepted increment, $a_t^2\le cA_t$ because
$\mathcal L_t\ge\mathcal L_0$.
Write $s_t=\sqrt{A_t/c}$. Then
$s_t^2-s_{t-1}^2=a_t/c\le s_t$, so
$s_t-s_{t-1}\le s_t/(s_t+s_{t-1})\le1$.
The denominator is positive for an accepted step.
Starting from $s_0=0$ gives $s_n\le n$ and $A_n\le cn^2$.

Each rejection visits a different dyadic curvature level
$\mathcal L_0\,2^r$ because the candidate doubles on rejection
and never decreases. Its current accepted mass is at most $A_n$.
The explicit positive-root formula in \eqref{eq:preconf-weight}
therefore gives
$a_j\le c2^{-r}+\sqrt{cA_n}\,2^{-r/2}$.
Sum these bounds over the subset of levels actually rejected, and
then over all $r\ge0$. The two geometric sums are $2$ and
$(1-2^{-1/2})^{-1}=2+\sqrt2$.
Accepted increments sum to $A_n$, proving the first account.
Substitute $A_n\le cN^2$ for the second.

label: thm:preconf-error-contract
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Pre-step acceleration on a simultaneous error event

title: Proof
body_md:
The center identity is
$A_j^+(x_j^+-y_j)=a_jw_j$.
Smoothness and the two error bounds imply
\[
 A_j^+[\widehat q_j-\langle g_j,x_j^+-y_j\rangle]
 \le\frac{h_0L_\phi}{2\mathcal L_j}\lVert w_j\rVert^2
                   +a_j\eta_j\lVert w_j\rVert.
\]
At $\mathcal L_j\ge2L_\phi$ the first term is at most
$h_0\lVert w_j\rVert^2/4$. The elementary square inequality gives
$a_j\eta_j\lVert w_j\rVert\le
h_0\lVert w_j\rVert^2/4+a_j^2\eta_j^2/h_0$.
Thus this trial passes. Rejections occur only below $2L_\phi$;
their doubling gives a candidate below $4L_\phi$.
Monotonicity proves the rejection count and ceiling, including $L_\phi=0$.
The cap condition then ensures completion.
For accepted increments, $a_t=\sqrt{h_0A_t/\mathcal L_t}$, so
\[
 \sqrt{A_t}-\sqrt{A_{t-1}}
 =\frac{a_t}{\sqrt{A_t}+\sqrt{A_{t-1}}}
 \ge\frac12\sqrt{h_0/\overline{\mathcal L}}.
\]
Summing proves the denominator bound.

Projection optimality gives
\[
 a_j\langle g_j,v_j^+-u\rangle
 \le\frac{h_0}{2}
   [\lVert u-v^-\rVert^2-\lVert u-v_j^+\rVert^2-\lVert w_j\rVert^2].
\]
Convexity at $y_j$ gives
$A^-\phi(x^-)+a_j\phi(u)\ge
A_j^+\phi(y_j)+a_j\langle \nabla\phi(y_j),u-v^-\rangle$.
Combine these two inequalities and the center identity. The increase
of the potential
$A[\phi(x)-\phi(u)]+h_0\lVert u-v\rVert^2/2$ is at most
\[
 A_j^+[\phi(x_j^+)-\phi(y_j)-\langle g_j,x_j^+-y_j\rangle]
 -\frac{h_0}{2}\lVert w_j\rVert^2
 +a_j\langle e_j,u-v^-\rangle.
\]
Substitute the accepted model test and the definition of $\zeta_j^q$.
The increase is at most $\chi_j+Z_j(u)$.
Only accepted states change the potential, so these transitions
telescope. The inequality
$f(x_n)-f(u)\le\phi(x_n)-\phi(u)+\beta_\gamma(u)$ proves
\eqref{eq:preconf-potential}.

Under \eqref{eq:preconf-tolerance},
$\chi_j\le a_j\varepsilon/4$.
Both $u-v^-$ and $w_j$ have norm at most $D$, hence
$|Z_j(u)|\le a_jD(\eta_j^g+\eta_j^q)
\le a_j\varepsilon/4$.
Accepted weights sum to $A_N$. Discard the nonnegative terminal
distance in \eqref{eq:preconf-potential}, divide by the positive
$A_N$, and use its deterministic lower bound. This proves
\eqref{eq:preconf-unweighted} without centering selected errors.

label: thm:preconf-paid-risk
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Expected risk with confidence bounds

title: Proof
body_md:
Condition on the history preceding each batch. Its center, accuracy
bound and integer block size are fixed before its samples are drawn.
Lemma~\ref{lem:preconf-robust-means} and
\eqref{eq:preconf-block-number} bound each of the at most
$2K_{\rm tr}$ conditional failure probabilities by
$\delta_{\rm conf}/(2K_{\rm tr})$.
An executed-trial indicator is predictable before its first batch;
the tentative comparison pair is known before its second batch.
Taking expectations of these conditional bounds and summing gives
failure probability at most $\delta_{\rm conf}$. This union is over the
executed sequence, rather than hypothetical center locations.

On the joint event, Theorem~\ref{thm:preconf-error-contract}
guarantees completion and \eqref{eq:preconf-unweighted}.
On its complement the output remains feasible and
$f(\widehat x)-f(u)\le MD$.
The good-event upper bound is nonnegative, since $\beta_\gamma(u)\ge0$.
Splitting the expectation over the two events proves
\eqref{eq:preconf-expected-risk}. Neither conditional centering of the
robust aggregate nor division by a random failed-execution weight
is invoked.

The vector and scalar blocks use separate independent sampled
functions, each evaluated at exactly two points. All vector records can be drawn
in one parallel stage. After their aggregate determines the
projection, all comparison records can be drawn in the next stage.
There is one projection per trial. This proves the exact counts.
For any split $\theta\in(0,1)$, the continuous block-size bound is
$c_g/\theta^2+c_q/(1-\theta)^2$. Its derivative vanishes only at
$\theta=\theta_g$, and its second derivative is positive.
Substitution gives the minimum $\Lambda_{\rm mom}$.
The ceilings in \eqref{eq:preconf-block-sizes} therefore imply
$b_j^g+b_j^q\le2+\Lambda_{\rm mom}/\eta_j^2$.
The reciprocal of the squared tolerance is
$\max\{16D^2/\varepsilon^2,4a_j/(h_0\varepsilon)\}$,
proving \eqref{eq:preconf-realized-budget}.
Finally bound each maximum by its two-term sum, use
$J_{\rm exec}\le K_{\rm tr}$ and apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:preconf-weight-account}. This proves the deterministic
budget bound determined before sampling. The good-event rejection count proves the last
stage and projection bounds.

label: cor:preconf-public-cap
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:preconf-public-cap}
Suppose the supplied $\overline M_2$ also bounds the sample
weak-gradient and segment assumptions, or the random sample Lipschitz
assumption, on the evaluation domain. Then one may set
\begin{align}
 K_{\rm tr}&=N+
  \lceil \log_2\max\{1,2\sqrt d\,\overline M_2/
                               (\gamma\mathcal L_0)\}\rceil,\nonumber\\
 \delta_{\rm conf}&=\min\{1/2,\varepsilon/(4\overline M_2D)\}.
 \label{eq:preconf-fully-public-cap}
\end{align}
No population smoothness or original-distance input is used. The
expected risk obeys
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[f(\widehat x)-f(u)]
 \le\frac{2\max\{\mathcal L_0,4L_\phi\}R_u^2}{N^2}
                  +\frac{3\varepsilon}{4}+\beta_\gamma(u),
 \label{eq:preconf-fully-public-risk}
\end{equation}
where $L_\phi$ can be any valid smoothness constant of $\phi$.
For an originally $L$-smooth population, one may take $L_\phi\le L$.
Consequently the population-dependent sufficient condition
$2\max\{\mathcal L_0,4L_\phi\}R_u^2/N^2+\beta_\gamma(u)
\le\varepsilon/4$ gives expected gap at most $\varepsilon$.
This condition is used in the analysis and does not define a stopping
rule. The exact and deterministic budget bounds of
Theorem~\ref{thm:preconf-paid-risk} apply.

name: A trial cap chosen before sampling for ball smoothing

title: Proof
body_md:
Under the sample Lipschitz assumption, taking expectations of sample
differences gives population Lipschitz constant at most
$\mathbb E m(\xi)\le\overline M_2$.
Under the weak-gradient and segment assumptions, integrate along a
fixed segment and use
$\mathbb E\lVert \nabla F(z,\xi)\rVert
\le(\mathbb E\lVert \nabla F(z,\xi)\rVert^2)^{1/2}\le\overline M_2$.
Its stated integrability and continuity give the same inequality,
including boundary endpoints. Hence $M\le\overline M_2$ may be used.
The ball-smoothing bound supplies the valid constant
$\sqrt d\,\overline M_2/\gamma$.
For any other valid $L_\phi$, their minimum is also valid.
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:preconf-paid-risk} with this minimum;
the cap chosen before sampling in \eqref{eq:preconf-fully-public-cap} is then at
least $N+J_\star$, and its curvature ceiling is at most
$\max\{\mathcal L_0,4L_\phi\}$. Also
$\delta_{\rm conf} MD\le\varepsilon/4$.
Apply \eqref{eq:preconf-expected-risk} and the sufficient condition.
The cap and confidence parameters depend only on the displayed
supplied inputs and moment bound.

label: thm:observable-certification-cost
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:observable-certification-cost}
Under the null law $Z=0$, let
$C=\{\tau<\infty,\widehat U\le\eta\}$, where $\eta>0$, and let
$q=\Pr_0(C)>0$. For $\mu>\eta$ and $0<p<1$, define the alternative
\[
 Z=\frac{\mu}{p}\,\xi,\qquad \xi\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p).
\]
Its mean is $\mu$ and its second moment is $\mu^2/p$.
The alternative false-report probability satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \Pr_1(\tau<\infty,\mu>\widehat U)
 \ge\mathbb E_0[\mathbf1_C(1-p)^\tau]
 \ge q\exp\left(
   \frac{\log(1-p)}{q}\,
   \mathbb E_0[\tau\mathbf1_C]\right).
 \label{eq:observable-certification-coupling}
\end{equation}
The second bound is interpreted as zero if the restricted expectation
is infinite. If \eqref{eq:observable-certification-validity} holds on
this alternative and $q>\delta_{\rm conf}$, then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_0[\tau\mathbf1_C]
 \ge\frac{q\log(q/\delta_{\rm conf})}{-\log(1-p)}.
 \label{eq:observable-certification-price}
\end{equation}
The result covers arbitrary endpoints, adaptive batches and stopping,
and any number of sequential sampling stages.
head: environment
name: Adaptive certification cost on the common history

title: Proof
body_md:
Couple the internal seed on the two populations, including all
independent direction choices. Under the null, every realized
function is identically zero, so the entire transcript, terminal
bound and sample count are functions of this seed. Prepare an infinite
independent Bernoulli sequence for the alternative. For each null
seed in $C$, the event that its first $\tau$ Bernoulli variables
vanish has probability $(1-p)^\tau$. On this event every complete
sample function agrees with the null, at every possible endpoint.
Induction through the adaptive transcript therefore identifies all
queries, batches, decisions and the terminal report with the null
execution. The reported bound is at most $\eta<\mu$, so it is false.
Integration over the seed proves the first inequality in
\eqref{eq:observable-certification-coupling}. This argument uses
only the samples drawn before the null report and requires no
deterministic horizon.

Conditional on $C$, the function $t\mapsto(1-p)^t$ is convex.
If $\mathbb E_0[\tau\mid C]<\infty$, Jensen gives the second bound.
If that expectation is infinite, its stated zero bound is immediate.
When validity holds and $q>\delta_{\rm conf}$, comparison with $\delta_{\rm conf}$, taking
logarithms and dividing by $-\log(1-p)>0$ gives
\eqref{eq:observable-certification-price}; an infinite restricted
expectation also satisfies it.

label: cor:observable-certification-no-cap
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: No finite upper confidence bound without a moment bound

title: Proof
body_md:
For each integer $k\ge1$, let
$C_k=\{\tau<\infty,\widehat U\le k\}$.
Choose the alternative mean $\mu=k+1$ and let $p\downarrow0$.
Every alternative has finite second moment, so validity and
Theorem~\ref{thm:observable-certification-cost} imply
$\mathbb E_0[\mathbf1_{C_k}(1-p)^\tau]\le\delta_{\rm conf}$.
On $C_k$, $\tau$ is finite. Dominated convergence therefore gives
$\Pr_0(C_k)\le\delta_{\rm conf}$. The increasing union of the $C_k$ is the
event in \eqref{eq:observable-certification-no-cap}.
Continuity from below completes the proof.

label: thm:observable-certification-capped
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:observable-certification-capped}
Suppose validity is required on the class $\mathbb E Z^2\le \overline M_2^2$,
where the common cap $\overline M_2>0$ is supplied. If $0<\eta<\overline M_2$ and
$C=\{\tau<\infty,\widehat U\le\eta\}$ and
$q=\Pr_0(C)>\delta_{\rm conf}$, then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_0[\tau\mathbf1_C]
 \ge\frac{q\log(q/\delta_{\rm conf})}
 {-\log(1-\eta^2/\overline M_2^2)}.
 \label{eq:observable-certification-capped-lower}
\end{equation}
In particular, when $\overline M_2^2\ge2\eta^2$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_0[\tau\mathbf1_C]
 \ge\frac{q \overline M_2^2}{2\eta^2}\log(q/\delta_{\rm conf}).
 \label{eq:observable-certification-capped-order}
\end{equation}

Conversely, for any $\delta_{\rm conf}\in(0,1)$, set
$b=\lceil8\overline M_2^2/\eta^2\rceil$ and let $k$ be the smallest positive
odd integer with $k\ge2\log_2(1/\delta_{\rm conf})$.
Draw $bk$ records in $k$ disjoint blocks of size $b$, let $m$ be
the median of their block averages, and report
$\widehat U=m+\eta$. This bound has validity at least $1-\delta_{\rm conf}$
uniformly over the stated class, and under the null it satisfies
$\widehat U=\eta$ surely. It uses exactly $bk$ independent pairs,
$2bk$ values, and one sampling stage at a fixed pair of centers.
For $\overline M_2^2\ge2\eta^2$ and $\delta_{\rm conf}\le1/4$, this matches the necessary
$\overline M_2^2\eta^{-2}\log(1/\delta_{\rm conf})$ order for $q=1$, even though the
null law has zero actual variance.
head: environment
name: The certification scale under a supplied moment cap

title: Proof
body_md:
For every $\mu\in(\eta,\overline M_2)$ choose $p=\mu^2/\overline M_2^2$ in
Theorem~\ref{thm:observable-certification-cost}. The resulting law
has second moment exactly $\overline M_2^2$. Let $\mu\downarrow\eta$ in its
necessary cost inequality to obtain
\eqref{eq:observable-certification-capped-lower}.
For $x=\eta^2/\overline M_2^2\le1/2$,
$-\log(1-x)=\int_0^x(1-t)^{-1}\,dt\le2x$, proving
\eqref{eq:observable-certification-capped-order}.

For the upper construction, the variance of each block average is
at most $\overline M_2^2/b\le\eta^2/8$. Chebyshev therefore bounds its
probability of deviating by more than $\eta$ from the mean by $1/8$.
If the median deviates by more than $\eta$, at least $(k+1)/2$
blocks are bad. Their independence and a union bound over subsets
give failure probability at most
\[
 2^k(1/8)^{(k+1)/2}
 =2^{-k/2-3/2}\le2^{-k/2}\le\delta_{\rm conf}.
\]
Thus $m+\eta$ is an upper mean bound with the stated coverage.
Under the null, every block average is zero, giving the asserted
report and $q=1$. All $bk$ functions can be sampled in parallel and evaluated at the
same fixed pair of centers. Each sampled function is evaluated twice.
Finally, $b\le8\overline M_2^2/\eta^2+1$ and
$k<2\log_2(1/\delta_{\rm conf})+2$ show the matching order.

label: lem:universal-distance-family
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: A common-curvature family

title: Proof
body_md:
The mean of the added linear term under $\mathbb P_1$ is $LDx$.
Expanding the square proves the population formulas and the two
stationary minimizers. If $\xi$ indicates a rare label, the centered
gradient under $\mathbb P_1$ is $LD(T\xi-1)$. Its variance is
$L^2D^2(T-1)$, independently of the query point. Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_0|F_0'(x)|^2=L^2(x-D)^2,\qquad
 \mathbb E_1|F'(x)|^2=L^2x^2+L^2D^2(T-1).
\]
On $J$, $|x-D|<3D$ and $|x|<3D$, proving the stated Lipschitz
and moment bounds. Maximizing the two displayed expressions over
$[-D,2D]$ gives the exact closed-interval envelopes. All second
derivatives equal $L$.

label: thm:universal-distance-pareto
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:universal-distance-pareto}
Consider any randomized adaptive procedure drawing at most $T$ independent
sampled functions from the family in Lemma~\ref{lem:universal-distance-family}
and returning a feasible output $X\in Q$. Its supplied inputs and
internal seed law are the same on the two populations. Each draw may
reveal the entire sampled function; queries, stopping decisions and
sampling schedules may be adaptive. Let $X_0$ denote its output under
$\mathbb P_0$ and put
\[
 \varepsilon_i=\mathbb E_i[f_i(X)-f_i(x_i^\star)],\qquad
 q_T=(1-1/T)^T.
\]
Then $q_T\ge1/4$ and
\begin{equation}
 \varepsilon_1\ge q_T\frac L2\mathbb E_0X_0^2
 \ge q_T\frac L2
       \left(D-\sqrt{2\varepsilon_0/L}\right)_+^2.
 \label{eq:universal-distance-pareto}
\end{equation}
The statement includes arbitrary nonsymmetric two-value queries and
does not depend on their number of sequential sampling stages.
head: environment
name: A universal cross-instance risk relation

title: Proof
body_md:
Couple the algorithm's internal random seed on the two laws. Prepare
$T$ independent rare indicators for the alternative law, assigning
them to sampled functions in their order of use; pad an early stop with
unused indicators. The event $E$ that all $T$ indicators are zero has
probability $q_T$ and is independent of the seed. On $E$, every
revealed function is exactly $F_0$. Induction through the adaptive
transcript therefore identifies all queries, internal decisions and
the final output with the deterministic-law execution. This also
covers endpoints chosen adaptively within a same-sample pair.

The alternative excess risk is $LX^2/2$ and is nonnegative on every
transcript. Restricting its expectation to $E$ proves the first
inequality. Under the deterministic law,
$2\varepsilon_0/L=\mathbb E_0(D-X_0)^2$. Since $0\le X_0\le D$,
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
$\mathbb E_0X_0\ge D-\sqrt{2\varepsilon_0/L}$, while Jensen gives
$\mathbb E_0X_0^2\ge(\mathbb E_0X_0)^2$. This proves the second inequality.
Compactness ensures all moments used here are finite.

For the probability estimate, set $g(x)=x\log(1-1/x)$ for $x\ge2$.
With $u=1/(x-1)$ its derivative is $u-\log(1+u)\ge0$, because
$\log(1+u)=\int_0^u(1+s)^{-1}\,ds\le u$.
Thus $q_T=\exp(g(T))\ge\exp(g(2))=1/4$.

label: thm:universal-distance-menu
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: An exact competitive factor on the two-law family

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $z=\mathbb E_0X_0$. Jensen and
Theorem~\ref{thm:universal-distance-pareto} give
\[
 \varepsilon_0\ge\frac L2(D-z)^2,\qquad
 \varepsilon_1\ge q_T\frac L2z^2.
\]
Hence $\varepsilon_i\le Cb_i$ implies
\[
 D-z\le\sqrt{2Cb_0/L},\qquad
 z\le\sqrt{2Cb_1/(q_TL)}.
\]
Adding and squaring proves the lower bound in
\eqref{eq:universal-distance-menu-factor}.

For attainment, query endpoints $0,D$ for each of $T$ independently
sampled functions. For the common function, the difference is $-LD^2/2$; for the
rare function, the difference is $-LD^2/2+LD^2T$. Thus any occurrence of the rare function is
identified exactly. If at least one is observed, output zero.
Otherwise output the feasible point
\[
 z_* =\frac{D\sqrt{b_1}}
 {\sqrt{b_1}+\sqrt{q_Tb_0}}.
\]
The deterministic-law risk is $L(D-z_*)^2/2$ and the alternative-law
risk is $q_TLz_*^2/2$. Substitution shows that both benchmark ratios
are $C_*$. All pairs can be sampled in one stage.

label: cor:universal-distance-variance
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: A local accelerated variance benchmark

title: Proof
body_md:
The two benchmarks are
\[
 b_0^{\rm var}=\frac{L(D-r)^2}{N^2},\qquad
 b_1^{\rm var}=\frac{Lr^2}{N^2}
                  +LDr\sqrt{1-1/T}\le2LDr.
\]

Otherwise $\varepsilon_0<LD^2/8$, so
\eqref{eq:universal-distance-pareto} gives
$\varepsilon_1\ge q_TLD^2/8\ge LD^2/32$.
Dividing by $b_1^{\rm var}\le2LDr$ gives $C\ge D/(64r)$.
These alternatives prove
\eqref{eq:universal-distance-variance-price}.

Formula~\eqref{eq:universal-distance-menu-factor} is bounded above
by $LD^2/(2b_0^{\rm var})$ and by
$q_TLD^2/(2b_1^{\rm var})$. For $r\le D/2$ the first bound is
at most $2N^2$. For $T\ge2$,
$b_1^{\rm var}\ge LDr/\sqrt2$, so the second bound is at most
$D/r$. This proves the upper bound in
\eqref{eq:universal-distance-variance-match}.

label: cor:universal-distance-moment
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: A local second-moment benchmark

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $a=N^{-2}+3T^{-1/2}$. Since
$b_0^{\rm mom}\le LD^2a$, either $C\ge1/(8a)$, which gives
$C\ge\min\{N^2,\sqrt T\}/32$, or

       +LDr\sqrt{1+8/T}\le(1+\sqrt3)LDr\le3LDr,

 b_0^{\rm mom}\ge\frac{LD^2}{4N^2},\qquad
 b_0^{\rm mom}\ge\frac{3LD^2}{2\sqrt T},\qquad
 b_1^{\rm mom}\ge LDr.

\eqref{eq:universal-distance-menu-factor} to obtain
$C_*^{\rm mom}\le\min\{2N^2,\sqrt T/3,D/(2r)\}$, proving
the stated upper bound.

label: thm:trajectory
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:trajectory}
Let $f\le\phi_{t+1}\le\phi_t$ be predictably chosen differentiable convex targets with
common gradient Lipschitz bound $L_*<\infty$. Assume that the total
errors $e_t^y,e_t^x$ are integrable. For $\iota\in\{y,x\}$, define
$b_t^\iota=\mathbb E[e_t^\iota\mid\mathcal F_t^\iota]$ and
$\zeta_t^\iota=e_t^\iota-b_t^\iota$, where $v_{t-1}$ is
$\mathcal F_t^y$-measurable and $v_t-v_{t-1}$ is
$\mathcal F_t^x$-measurable. For fixed $u\in Q$,
put $R_u=\lVert u-x^0\rVert$ and
$\mathcal S_N(u)=A_N^{-1}\sum_t t\,\mathbb E[\phi_t(u)-f(u)]$.
Assume $\mathcal S_N(u)<\infty$ and $\mathbb E\mathcal E_N<\infty$.
Then
\begin{align}
 &\mathbb E[f(x_N)-f(u)]
 \le\frac{h_0R_u^2}{2A_N}+\mathcal S_N(u)\nonumber\\*
 &\quad+\frac1{A_N}\min\left\{
 \begin{aligned}
  &4D^2\mathbb E\mathcal C_N+2\sqrt2D\sqrt{\mathbb E\mathcal E_N},\\
  &8L_*D^2+2D\sqrt{\mathbb E\mathcal E_N}
 \end{aligned}\right\}\nonumber\\*
 &\quad+\frac D{A_N}\sum_t t\,\mathbb E(\lVert b_t^y\rVert+\lVert b_t^x\rVert).
 \label{eq:trajectory-risk-main}
\end{align}
The full proof is in Appendix~\ref{subsec:proof-trajectory}.

label: cor:weighted-variance
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:weighted-variance}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:trajectory}, let each update
estimate be the average of records that are conditionally independent
given its pre-update history. Each batch size and center is measurable
with respect to that history, and $\mathcal F_t^x$ contains
$\mathcal F_t^y$ and the first update batch. Assume each record has conditional mean
$\nabla\phi_t(y_t)$ or $\nabla\phi_t(x_t)$ at its corresponding center.
In particular, exact records of \eqref{eq:record} satisfy this condition
when $\phi_t=f_{\gamma_t}$. Let $V_t^y$ and $V_t^x$ be the conditional
single-record variances at $y_t$ and $x_t$, respectively, at the selected
radius and before the corresponding update records. Define
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal V_N=\sum_t t^2\mathbb E\left(
       \frac{V_t^y}{B_t^y}+\frac{V_t^x}{B_t^x}\right).
 \label{eq:weighted-variance-main}
\end{equation}
Then $\mathbb E\mathcal E_N=\mathcal V_N$ and the risk bound
\eqref{eq:trajectory-risk-main} holds with no bias term and with
$\mathcal V_N$ as its error energy. The full proof is in
Appendix~\ref{subsec:proof-weighted-variance}.

label: prop:smoothed-distance
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:smoothed-distance}
Let $d=2$, $\gamma>0$ and $0<\theta\le1/1000$. Define
\[
 f_\theta(x,y)=\max\{\theta^2|x|,|y|,2y-\theta x\},
 \qquad
 Q_\theta=[-3\gamma/\theta,3\gamma/\theta]\times[-3\gamma,3\gamma],
 \qquad x^0=(0,\gamma).
\]
The objective is globally $\sqrt5$-Lipschitz and convex, and its
unique minimizer on $Q_\theta$ is $(0,0)$, with $R=\gamma$.
Every minimizer $(x_\gamma,y_\gamma)$ on $Q_\theta$ of its uniform
ball smoothing satisfies
\begin{equation}
 x_\gamma>\gamma/(8\theta).
 \label{eq:smoothed-minimizer-far}
\end{equation}
Consequently the distance from $x^0$ to a smoothed minimizer cannot
be bounded by a universal multiple of $R+\gamma$, even for
deterministic convex Lipschitz samples on a compact feasible set.
head: environment
name: Ball smoothing and minimizer distance

title: Proof
body_md:
Each displayed function in the maximum is convex. Their Lipschitz
constants are $\theta^2$, one and $\sqrt{4+\theta^2}$, so their
maximum is $\sqrt5$-Lipschitz. Since
$f_\theta\ge\max\{\theta^2|x|,|y|\}$, it is nonnegative and
equals zero only at $(0,0)$, which belongs to $Q_\theta$.
The smoothed function is finite and continuous and therefore has
a minimum on the compact set $Q_\theta$.

Let $U$ be uniform on the unit disk. Its second-coordinate density is
\[
 p(u)=\frac2\pi\sqrt{1-u^2},\qquad -1\le u\le1.
\]
This follows by integrating the constant disk density $1/\pi$
over the horizontal section of length $2\sqrt{1-u^2}$.
Set $b(y)=\mathbb E|y+\gamma U_2|$. This function is convex, even and
minimized at zero. Differentiating its one-dimensional integral
gives $b'(0)=0$ and
$b''(y)=2p(y/\gamma)/\gamma$ for $|y|<\gamma$.
On $0\le y\le\gamma/4$ the density is at least
$\sqrt{15}/(2\pi)$. Integration of the second derivative and
monotonicity of the even convex function thus give
\begin{equation}
 b(y)-b(0)\ge\frac{\sqrt{15}}{32\pi}\gamma
 \quad\text{whenever }|y|\ge\gamma/4.
 \label{eq:smoothed-base-shift}
\end{equation}

Suppose $x\le\gamma/(8\theta)$ and $|y|<\gamma/4$.
On the event $U_2\in[1/2,3/4]$, put
$z=y+\gamma U_2$ and $s=\theta(x+\gamma U_1)$. Since
$|U_1|\le1$ and $\theta\le1/16$,
\[
 z\ge\gamma/4,\qquad
 s\le\gamma/8+\theta\gamma\le3\gamma/16.
\]
Therefore $2z-s\ge|z|+\gamma/16$ on this event. Its probability
is at least
\[
 \int_{1/2}^{3/4}p(u)\,du\ge\frac{\sqrt7}{8\pi}.
\]
The objective always dominates $|z|$, so
\begin{equation}
 f_{\theta,\gamma}(x,y)
 \ge b(y)+\frac{\sqrt7}{128\pi}\gamma
 \ge b(0)+\frac{\sqrt7}{128\pi}\gamma.
 \label{eq:smoothed-far-lower}
\end{equation}
For $|y|\ge\gamma/4$, inequality
\eqref{eq:smoothed-base-shift} gives a stronger bound. Hence
\eqref{eq:smoothed-far-lower} holds for every $y$ whenever
$x\le\gamma/(8\theta)$.

The comparison point $(2\gamma/\theta,0)$ belongs to $Q_\theta$.
For every $U$ in the unit disk, there
\[
 s=\theta(2\gamma/\theta+\gamma U_1)\ge(2-\theta)\gamma\ge\gamma,
 \qquad z=\gamma U_2\in[-\gamma,\gamma].
\]
Thus $2z-s\le|z|$, while
$\theta^2|2\gamma/\theta+\gamma U_1|\le(2\theta+\theta^2)\gamma$.
The inequality $\max\{a,b\}\le a+b$ for $a,b\ge0$ yields
\begin{equation}
 f_{\theta,\gamma}(2\gamma/\theta,0)
 \le b(0)+(2\theta+\theta^2)\gamma.
 \label{eq:smoothed-far-upper}
\end{equation}
Here $2\theta+\theta^2\le2001/10^6<1/256$, whereas
$\sqrt7/(128\pi)>1/256$ because $\sqrt7>2$ and $\pi<4$.
Consequently \eqref{eq:smoothed-far-upper} is strictly smaller
than \eqref{eq:smoothed-far-lower}; no constrained minimizer
can have $x\le\gamma/(8\theta)$.
Its distance from $x^0=(0,\gamma)$ is at least its positive
first coordinate. Dividing this distance by $R+\gamma=2\gamma$
and letting $\theta$ decrease to zero proves the final assertion.

label: thm:startup-noise-price
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: The cost of preserving the affine error bound

title: Proof
body_md:
The deterministic error bound gives
$\mathbb E_0\widehat x\ge r_0(1+A/2)-b_0$. Generate $n$ independent sampled functions
in advance, including unused functions if the algorithm stops early. Couple
the algorithm's internal randomness across the two instances. On the
event that every function from the second law is $F_0$, the full functions agree.
Induction through the adaptive transcript therefore gives the same
endpoints, batch allocations, stopping decisions and output. This event
is independent of the algorithm's internal randomness and has probability
$q=(1-1/n)^n$. The rare gap is $(1+1/n)\widehat x\ge0$, so restriction
to this event proves \eqref{eq:startup-affine-lower}.

label: cor:startup-price
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: The required stochastic error multiplier

title: Proof
body_md:
Theorem~\ref{thm:startup-noise-price} bounds the rare-instance risk
with $q=(1-1/n)^n$.
To bound the event probability directly, let
$g(x)=x\log(1-1/x)$ for $x\ge2$ and $z=1/(x-1)$. Then
\[
 g'(x)=z-\log(1+z)\ge0,
 \qquad \log(1+z)=\int_0^z(1+s)^{-1}\,ds\le z.
\]
Thus $q\ge\exp(g(2))=1/4$.

Since $R=r_0$ and $\sigma_1\le2\sqrt n$, the upper bound in
\eqref{eq:startup-local-contract} is at most
$r_0/(2A)+4Pr_0$. For $b_0=0$, the lower bound is at least
$r_0(1/4+A/8)$, yielding
\[
 4P\ge A/8+1/4-1/(2A)\ge A/8,
\]
because $A\ge3$. Hence $P\ge A/32$. For $b_0\le r_0A/4$,
the lower risk is at least $r_0(1/4+A/16)$; the same calculation
gives $P\ge A/64$.

label: lem:sphere-hiding
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sphere-hiding}
Let $\vartheta$ be uniform on the unit sphere in $\mathbb R^d$ and let $w$
be a deterministic unit vector. For $0<\beta<1$,
\[
 \mathbb P\bigl(|\langle \vartheta,w\rangle|>\beta\bigr)
 \le2\exp(-d\beta^2/2).
\]
head: environment
name: Spherical hiding

title: Proof
body_md:
By rotational invariance, take $w=(1,0,\ldots,0)$. Let $Z$ have independent
standard normal coordinates. Polar coordinates in its
rotation-invariant density show that $Z/\lVert Z\rVert$ is uniform on the
sphere and independent of $\lVert Z\rVert$. Integration by parts in the
one-dimensional normal density gives
$\mathbb E Z_1^{2k}=(2k-1)!!$ for integers $k\ge1$. The radial density is
proportional to $r^{d-1}e^{-r^2/2}$; integration by parts gives
$\mathbb E\lVert Z\rVert^{2k}=d(d+2)\cdots(d+2k-2)$. Independence therefore yields
\[
 \mathbb E\vartheta_1^{2k}
 =\frac{(2k-1)!!}{d(d+2)\cdots(d+2k-2)}
 \le\frac{(2k-1)!!}{d^k}.
\]
Symmetry implies
$\mathbb E e^{\lambda\vartheta_1}=\mathbb E\cosh(\lambda\vartheta_1)$.
Expand its nonnegative even-power series and use monotone convergence:
\[
 \mathbb E e^{\lambda\vartheta_1}
 \le\sum_{k=0}^\infty
       \frac{\lambda^{2k}(2k-1)!!}{(2k)!\,d^k}
 =e^{\lambda^2/(2d)}.
\]
The $k=0$ term is one. Markov's inequality with $\lambda=d\beta$
gives $\mathbb P(\vartheta_1>\beta)\le e^{-d\beta^2/2}$.
Apply symmetry and add the two tail bounds.

label: prop:hidden-band
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:hidden-band}
The objective $f_\vartheta$ is globally convex and $M$-Lipschitz.
Its minimum over $Q$ is $-\eta$, attained at $R\vartheta$, and
$f_\vartheta(0)=0$. For every $z\in\mathcal B_\vartheta$, regardless
of its norm,
\[
 |f_\vartheta(z)-g(z)|\le\Delta_{\eta,\beta}.
\]
This amplitude is attained at a point of $Q\cap\mathcal B_\vartheta$.
Every $z\in Q\cap\mathcal B_\vartheta$ has clean objective gap at least
$\eta(1-\beta)$.
head: environment
name: Hidden-direction geometry

title: Proof
body_md:
The support set in \eqref{eq:truncated-support} is nonempty and compact.
Its support function is convex and one-Lipschitz. The two terms in
\eqref{eq:hidden-objective} are convex and respectively $M$- and
$a$-Lipschitz. Since $a\le M/2$, their maximum is $M$-Lipschitz.

At $R\vartheta$, the support supremum is $\beta R$. It is attained by
$w=\beta\vartheta+\sqrt{1-\beta^2}\,w_\perp$, for any unit
$w_\perp\perp\vartheta$, which exists because $d\ge2$.
The two terms in \eqref{eq:hidden-objective} then both equal $-\eta$.
For every $z\in Q$, its linear term is at least $-aR=-\eta$,
so this is the minimum. At zero the maximum is zero.

For $z\ne0$ in the band, $w=z/\lVert z\rVert$ belongs to the support set;
thus $h_\vartheta(z)=\lVert z\rVert$. Put
$r=\lVert z\rVert$, $b=M(r-r_c)$ and $\ell=-a\langle \vartheta,z\rangle$.
Then
\[
 f_\vartheta(z)=\max\{b,\ell\},\qquad
 g(z)=\max\{b,0\},\qquad |\ell|\le a\beta r.
\]
If $r\le r_c$, then $g(z)=0$, while
$-a\beta r_c\le\ell\le\max\{b,\ell\}\le[\ell]_+\le a\beta r_c$.
If $r\ge r_c$, then $g(z)=b\ge0$. When $\ell\le b$, the
difference is zero. Otherwise it satisfies
\[
 \ell-b
 \le a\beta r-M(r-r_c)
 =a\beta r_c-(M-a\beta)(r-r_c)
 \le a\beta r_c.
\]
Here $M-a\beta\ge0$. Since
$a\beta r_c=\Delta_{\eta,\beta}$, this proves the bound uniformly
over all query norms; zero also satisfies it.

Take
$z=r_c[-\beta\vartheta+\sqrt{1-\beta^2}\,w_\perp]$.
Because $r_c\le R$, this point lies in $Q$, belongs to the band,
and has $b=0$ and $\ell=a\beta r_c$. It attains the amplitude.
Finally, on $Q\cap\mathcal B_\vartheta$,
$f_\vartheta(z)\ge-a\langle \vartheta,z\rangle\ge-\eta\beta$.
Subtract the minimum $-\eta$ to obtain the gap bound.

label: thm:work-noise
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:work-noise}
Fix an integer $T\ge0$, $0<\eta\le MR/2$ and $0<\beta\le1/2$.
For every randomized algorithm making at most $T$ original pairs and
returning a point of $Q$, there is an objective
$f_\vartheta$ and a fixed corruption of magnitude at most
$\Delta_{\eta,\beta}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[f_\vartheta(\widehat x)-\min_Q f_\vartheta]
 \ge\eta(1-\beta)
      [1-2(2T+1)e^{-d\beta^2/2}]_+.
 \label{eq:work-noise-lower}
\end{equation}
The objective is globally convex and $M$-Lipschitz. The result allows
arbitrary endpoints and any number of sequential stages, and remains
valid even when arbitrary points of $\mathbb R^d$ may be queried.
head: environment
name: Work under spatial corruption

title: Proof
body_md:
Draw the hidden direction $\vartheta$ uniformly and independently of
the algorithm's internal seed $\omega$. Run the algorithm against the
deterministic reference oracle $g$. Conditional on $\omega$, this
execution determines every endpoint and its final output independently
of $\vartheta$. Pad early stopping with endpoints at zero to obtain
$2T$ reference endpoints. Denote its output by $x_g(\omega)$.

Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:sphere-hiding} to every nonzero endpoint direction
and to the output direction. Zero lies in the band automatically.
A union bound shows, conditional on every seed, that all these
$2T+1$ points lie in $\mathcal B_\vartheta$ with probability at least
$1-2(2T+1)e^{-d\beta^2/2}$.

On this event the fixed oracle
$f_\vartheta+\delta_\vartheta$ agrees with $g$ at every reference
endpoint. Induction over the algorithm's decisions therefore shows
that its actual transcript, stopping time and output coincide with the
reference execution. The induction allows arbitrary pairs, parallel
groups selected from the preceding transcript, and even selection of
each next scalar endpoint after the preceding answer.

Proposition~\ref{prop:hidden-band} gives actual clean gap at least
$\eta(1-\beta)$ on the event. Outside it the gap is nonnegative.
Average over $\vartheta,\omega$ and replace a negative probability
bound by zero. At least one fixed direction attains the resulting
average lower bound on its expected gap. This objective and its fixed
corruption prove \eqref{eq:work-noise-lower}.

label: eq:noise-two-branches
title: Proof
body_md:
Put $\ell_T=\log(8(2T+1))$ and
$\beta_T=\sqrt{2\ell_T/d}$. The dimensional condition
$d\ge8\ell_T$ gives $\beta_T\le1/2$. The failure term in
\eqref{eq:work-noise-lower} is at most $1/4$, so its gap bound is
at least $3\eta/8$. The exact corruption amplitude is
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_{\eta,\beta_T}
 =\frac{2\eta\ell_T}{d}
  +\frac{\sqrt2\,\eta^2\sqrt{\ell_T}}{MR\sqrt d}.
 \label{eq:noise-two-branches}
\end{equation}
For $0<\varepsilon\le MR/8$, select $\eta=4\varepsilon$.
This is at most $MR/2$, and the expected gap lower bound is
$3\varepsilon/2$. Equation~\eqref{eq:noise-two-branches} becomes
$8\varepsilon\ell_T/d+
16\sqrt2\,\varepsilon^2\sqrt{\ell_T}/(MR\sqrt d)$.
Any allowed larger corruption includes this fixed constructed
corruption. This proves the stated impossibility. Since $D=2R$,
the second term also equals
$32\sqrt2\,\varepsilon^2\sqrt{\ell_T}/(MD\sqrt d)$.
\hfill$\square$

\label{cor:exponential-work}
Fix $0<\eta\le MR/2$. For an allowed $\Delta>0$, let
\[
 \beta_\Delta=\min\left\{\tfrac12,\sqrt{\Delta/(2\eta)},
                               MR\Delta/(2\eta^2)\right\}.
\]
If
\[
 T\le\frac1{16}\exp(d\beta_\Delta^2/2)-\frac12,
\]
some allowed fixed corrupted instance has expected gap at least
$3\eta/8$. Thus a uniform expected gap strictly below $3\eta/8$
requires strictly more pairs than this bound, and more than twice this
number of scalar values.
head: environment
name: Exponential work requirement

title: Proof
body_md:
The definition gives
$\eta\beta_\Delta^2\le\Delta/2$ and
$\eta^2\beta_\Delta/(MR)\le\Delta/2$.
Consequently \eqref{eq:exact-band-amplitude} is at most $\Delta$.
The stated pair condition is equivalent to
$2(2T+1)e^{-d\beta_\Delta^2/2}\le1/4$.
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:work-noise} and $1-\beta_\Delta\ge1/2$.

label: prop:bias-ambiguity
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:bias-ambiguity}
Fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Suppose the query domain is contained in $R_h\mathbb B_2^d$,
$R_h>0$, and the smoothing ball of radius $0<\gamma\le R_h$ is legal at
zero. For $0<a\le M$ with $aR_h\le\Delta$, the deterministic instances
\[
 f_0(z)=0,\quad\delta_0(z)=0,\qquad
 f_1(z)=a\lVert z\rVert,\quad
 \delta_1(z)=-\min\{a\lVert z\rVert,\Delta\}
\]
give identical observations at every legal endpoint. Their clean
smoothing biases at zero are respectively zero and $a\mu_d\gamma$.
Every upper confidence bound with coverage $1-\alpha$ for that clean bias
on both instances must therefore satisfy
\[
 \mathbb P_0(U_{\mathrm{bias}}\ge a\mu_d\gamma)\ge1-\alpha.
\]
This statement is independent of the number of original pairs and
sequential stages.
head: environment
name: Ambiguity in uncorrupted smoothing bias

title: Proof
body_md:
Both objectives are convex and $a$-Lipschitz, and both corruptions are
globally bounded by $\Delta$. On the query domain,
$a\lVert z\rVert\le aR_h\le\Delta$, so the observed functions are
identically zero. Every adaptive transcript and every output
statistic thus have the same law. For uniform ball $U$,
$f_{1,\gamma}(0)-f_1(0)=a\gamma\mathbb E\lVert U\rVert=a\mu_d\gamma$,
whereas the bias on the base instance vanishes. Apply the required
upper coverage on instance one and transfer the identical statistic
law to instance zero.
